location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: In March 2024, I told my readers about our ascent of Sri Lanka’s Adam Peak (aka Śrī Pāda or Adam’s Peak), which is in a mountainous area in Sabaragamuwa province. And I ended my post by saying that there are TWO Adam Peaks on the Island. The second is Little Adam's Peak (1,151 meters high), located near the town of Ella in Uva Province. Even then I read that climbing the "Little Adam" is even more interesting, as climbing is much easier, and the views from its summit are particularly interesting and colorful. And here I am, all so magical after EXACTLY ONE YEAR, fulfilled the dream of personal travel tablets – I am back in Ceylon, and I did climb Little Adam’s Peak!!! Although there are only 124 kilometres between Adam Peak and Adam Lesser Peak, the difference is stark: in the first you storm the MOUNTAIN, in the second you climb the HILL cheerfully. Although it must be acknowledged that Little Adam is a mountain that is part of the Badulla County mountain system. Where Little Adam's Peak came from - I never understood. There are several versions: one says it's after the "big brother" that the uniform resembles. Some argue that it is an Aboriginal marketing move to add to the attraction of the facility. Can the knowledgeable tell? From where we were stationed in Ella - apartments at the Meditation monastery Sri Sumanarama temple that's on Temple Road, Google maps gave four versts to the summit and a minimum of an hour of footdrilling. Since most of the route ran first through the city, and then along the hiking trail, they decided not to take a tuk-tuk to the foot and just stretch their legs. So after an early breakfast, they immediately moved on. The night mist and haze had just begun to clear, allowing for quite decent photos. The climb isn't really hard - there's no comparison to Adam's Peak. Therefore, it is even suitable for people far from mountaineering (as the author of these lines). On the way, and from the viewing platform itself, super atmospheric videos open up - I photographed tirelessly, afraid of missing all the interesting things. Revisiting the footage afterwards, he found that he had managed to photograph almost everything three or four times, but in that “moment of happiness” each frame was perceived as something new and interesting. On their way back they went through tea plantations that stretch on the slopes near the trail - a sight unusual and thus very interesting. A visit to Little Adam’s Peak is one of the most memorable events of our Sri Lankan trip. I recommend it!!!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Visiting Little Adam’s Peak was an absolutely amazing experience. The hike itself is gentle and accessible, making it perfect for anyone who enjoys a bit of adventure without it being too strenuous. As we climbed, we were surrounded by lush greenery, tea plantations, and the fresh mountain air, which made the journey incredibly refreshing. The view from the top is simply breathtaking rolling hills, valleys, and distant mountains stretch as far as the eye can see. It was the perfect spot to take a moment, soak in the scenery, and feel truly connected to nature. Our guide, Sithum, made the hike even more enjoyable. He shared interesting facts about the area, pointed out hidden viewpoints, and ensured that everyone in the group was comfortable and safe throughout the climb. Overall, Little Adam’s Peak is a must visit for anyone exploring Ella. It’s a mix of light adventure, stunning landscapes, and tranquility, and the experience will stay with you long after the hike is over.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We were expecting a slightly easier walk than it turned out to be, but it is an absolute must do when in Ella.  We walked from our homestay just outside the main street but you can get a tuk tuk for part of the way.  The walk is exposed so wear appropriate clothing or sunscreen, and take water. You will pass lots of small stalls on the way selling souvenirs at prices much cheaper than the main street but you will need small denominations to pay.  We did go on to the further peak (it's a bit of a goat track up the hill) and it is worth it for the extra views.  Good fun and took a little longer than expected. We walked from here back down an onto Nine Arches Bridge and then back into the town.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Aug 2025 • Family Neutral review. Visited Aug 22nd and just about to start the climb up when there was an exodus of people descending to escape a bee swarm attack. Two women carried down fireman style by staff who literally ran down the steps. Kudos to staff, they appeared to be doing a good job evacuating, especially the two chaps who carried wounded down. One women was very badly stung and taken away by ambulance. Another half dozen walking wounded taken by truck to hospital. Returned today after the rain and had a very quiet visit. Thunderstorm an hour before meant it was virtually deserted on top. Now the ‘could do better’. Apparently drones can set bees into swarm mode. No idea if this caused yesterday’s incident, but it is a risk. There is one sign prohibiting drones, but (a) it isn’t very prominent and doesn’t say why, and (b) there is no attempt at enforcement. I had sharp words with someone about to launch today, who had no idea of the risks (probably none today after the rain, but I wasn’t taking the chance) A few more (graphic) notices about why drones are banned would raise awareness. Positive: it’s a nice view. It’s not pristine wilderness: the zip line and swing and pool bar with thumping bass will not be to everyone’s liking. But I guess these things keep general access free and provide staff cover for incidents like yesterday. Worth a visit, but if allergic to bee stings I would not risk it (same story 9-arches bridge)

review_text: Little Adam's Peak is a popular hiking destination in Sri Lanka. Located in the Ella region, it offers stunning panoramic views of the surrounding countryside and tea plantations. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Mixed feelings about this one….. I would say that it is definitely a case of “should have been here 5 years ago” - maps show a mix of trails to L A P but these have now been gated off to steer you strictly past the super tacky and out of place pool club, cafe, zip line and rock climbing wall absolutely ruining the natural feel of an outdoor walk to a view point.  We were lucky in a way that we were just after sunrise so the Insta’s, sorry “content creators” were all on their way down as we were going up (roughly 6:30 am), we actually had the peak to ourselves (plus one coconut man) for a long while.  The walk to the highest peak is easy enough (all stairs), but the walk to the next peak is a tricky scramble up and down with no stairs or rails, just slippery dirt and rocks.  Views are nice from both peaks, depends whether you prefer a more distant view down to the coast (second peak) or a view featuring the second peak.  As we were coming back, more people were arriving and there was quite a crowd heading up (these were mostly tour group type people).  So despite missing the sunrise/ best light, we do feel like we got the best timing re having the peak to ourselves for so long. In summary a nice view and walk well on its way to being ruined.  Shame on the operators/ developers

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak was an experience that left me in awe of the breathtaking natural beauty. I ascended in solitude at 0500 to avoid the midday heat and crowds. The path wasn’t difficult to navigate since it was well marked and I could see it just fine as the first light came through. When I reached the top, I was rewarded with stunning panoramic views. It’s said to be a moderately difficult hike, but even with injured feet, I was able to ascend just fine. When I descended, I was able to see the surroundings of lush greenery, tea plantations, and rolling hills that I couldn’t really make out early in the morning. Little Adam's Peak is a gem of Sri Lanka's natural splendor. Highly recommend if you’re up for a moderate hike!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Eager to see what the "Little Adams peak" is like, I had to attempt the climb twice as in the first attempt somewhere halfway a sudden heavy downpour disrupted the journey. I had to hurriedly retreat to Flying Ravana ticketing centre for refuge. The thunderstorm lasted for about an hour and I gave up the idea of climbing and came to the pool club to spend the rest of the time. However, after the rain ceased the haze or the mist passed off and as there was some time to dusk, I decided to get back on the trail once again. This time I was well passed at least three quarters of the journey when the hell broke loose again drenching me severely. There was no shelter or a canopy for shade and the only option was to proceed until I reached the summit. Luckily for me there was no thunder or lightning. It was hazy at the beginning but with the ceasing of the rain it began to clear off, giving me good visibility of the surrounding mountain ranges and the distance water falls including the upper segment of "Ravana falls". My journey was well worth as the panoramic views were extremely beautiful. I had the best view of Ella gap and beyond. Up there I could not find any clue to why it is called little Adams peak, but there must be some legend behind it.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: If you're looking for a fun and easy climbing adventure in Kandy, then Little Peaks Adam is definitely worth checking out. The climb takes about 30 minutes and is relatively easy, but you'll want to wear good sneakers to ensure a steady grip on the rocks. There are three tops to the climb, with the last one being a bit more challenging to reach, but the incredible views of the valley and mountains in front of you make it all worth it. One of the best things about Little Peaks Adam is its location. The main entrance to the climb is only a 15-minute walk from Kandy village, making it easy to access and a great way to spend an afternoon. And once you reach the top, you'll be rewarded with panoramic views that will take your breath away. Overall, I highly recommend Little Peaks Adam for anyone looking for a fun and rewarding outdoor adventure in Kandy. The climb is easy enough for most people to enjoy, but still challenging enough to make you feel accomplished when you reach the top. And the views are simply stunning, making it an unforgettable experience.

review_text: This was a nice walk for sunrise – but a bit tough at times in the dark, especially if you’re rushing. It’s a bit of a tough walk on a narrow path between those two points – so don’t do it rushing, like we did… The sunset's a good one but if you're a seasoned traveller you'll likely have seen better - not a must-do for us.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is one of the must-do activities when visiting Ella. We were lucky that we booked and stayed at “Chillout Ella” Hotel where is located right at the entry point of the hiking. Hiking is relatively easy for anyone at all ages with good fitness level since most of the paths are not so steep and built with staircase. Generally, it took us about 45 mins or less to climb up to the top where it provides stunning panoramic views of the mountain ranges. There is no fee required to enter this hiking trail and zip line activities is available along the way for those who seek more adventurous fun! This activities can be combined with visiting to Nine Arch Bridge as there is a connecting path going to Nine Arch Bridge. A good 3 hours to be spent here or longer especially for nature trekking lovers!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This peak was within walking distance of our hotel (“98 Acres”).  Well marked route with gravel path and steps, some parts in shade but gets very hot so take plenty of water. Part way up there is a zip wire base station - two 550 metre lines across the valley, looked awesome, very well organised and safety standards seemed very good though we didn’t try it! Tip:  Go early in the morning for less crowded, less hot experience.

review_text: Myself, my husband and my parents (who are mid 70s) did this walk and although it isn’t hard it isn’t as easy as I had read either! The first half of the walk is lovely - on a gently sloping path with wonderful views.  The 2nd part of the walk was a bit more difficult with about 300 steps up to the top - it is fine if you pace yourself and take regular stops although I did find it hard going on my knees on the way down! The view is definitely worth it though, you get an amazing view of Ella Rock on the way up, and a 360 degree view once you are at the top.  On a good day I am told you can see as far as the Sea but it was a bit hazy the day we were there but you still had amazing views. I would definitely recommend going up - just pace yourself!

review_text: Trek up the Little Adam’s Peak, Ella One of the prettiest spots and most popular treks in Ella is up the Little Adam’s Peak.  However, we came across an unexpected hazard.  When we reached the point where the zipline takes off, we saw a sign posted which said, “drone cameras can trigger a bee attack.”  There were no drone cameras evident, but very soon there was a bee attack.  While we escaped, my driver waiting below said that about 20 people had to be taken to the hospital.  I believe the authorities need to take care of this.  If there are bees in the vicinity of this very popular spot and inclined to attack visitors, something must be done as a whole vacation can get ruined if one gets caught in a bee attack.  Till this is sorted out, the literature should also give some guidelines for persons on how to avoid the bee attack and how to respond in case of one.  One important thing I learnt by going through Google/Bing is that you never swat or try to fend off the bees but run as fast as you can and look for shelter.  In spite of the beautiful trek, the rating reflects the hazard which the tourists were subjected to.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk up to Little Adam’s Peak is doable by most people although those with mobility issues might give this one a pass. Easy flat first bit through tea plantation fields up to the zip line company office (where there are very clean toilets). Then the track gets more difficult and some scrambling is required. Over 300 steps/stairs and then the scrambling up to the top. However, the view is well worth the hike and the exercise is great for the legs and lungs. Once at the top you can go further but it is more difficult with a path that requires good strength and endurance. Total time to go up would be about an hour depending on your level of fitness. A must do!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The beginning of the walk is very gentle but after the zip line point it does become more challenging. Views from the top are breathtaking. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A nice hike with lovely views at every turn. Don’t believe the signs, it is considerably longer than the 500 m noted at the entry point. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: True enough that its a breathtaking view from the top of the Little Adams Peak at Ella but if you are a serious trekker challenge your self to do the real thing - the 5,500 step + tracking stretches of the Historical ADAMS PEAK that will take approx 3 - 4 hours from the base from one of the more popular access routes (Hatton - Nallathanniya / 4 hours away from Ella) Not only is it a thrilling experience with spectacular views along the way, the highlight is the sunrise from the eastern skies once you are at the peak which is absolutely breathtaking. For Sri Lankans Sri Pada assumes huge historic and religious importance and if you eventually decide to do it you will be treading along a path that was negotiated many centuries ago by historic travelers in the caliber of Buddhist traveler Fa Hien (411–12 CE) , Italian merchant / seafarer Marco Polo (1298 CE), Arab traveler Ibn Battuta (1344 CE) and in more recent history by John Davy, brother of the Sir Humphry Davy (1817 CE) The climbing season is considered to be from December to May. Off-season climbing is possible but considered more challenging and possibly best suited for seasoned trekkers. Best time of the day to climb the mountain will be starting from night, targeting to reach the top by early morning to view the sunrise My first experience in scaling Adams Peak was in 1988 at a teenager and i have repeated the feat couple of times there after close to those times. I have been trying to convince my family to do it a group since of late and is still to succeed.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We've just got back from a holiday in Sri Lanka that, both myself and my wife agree, is the best holiday we have ever had. We were meet at the airport by Rohan from Danulanka Tours, who would be our driver, photographer and tour guide for the next two weeks. The advantage of a local driver is not to be underestimated – as is the case in India, driving follows a set of rules that have no discernible pattern to drivers from other countries. Tolerances are measured in millimetres and cat-like reflexes are required that have been honed over many years. Rohan had an earlier career working as a photographer, which meant he was more than happy to take photographs at the various places we visited over the two weeks – a definite improvement over the clichéd selfie. Official tour guides in Sri Lanka are strictly controlled – you can be sure that any official guide will have a good knowledge of the history of any historical site in Sri Lanka. The additional benefits of a tour guide is they know when you need to arrive to get the most out your visit – whether that is to catch the ceremony at The Temple of the Tooth, or when you need to leave to get the view at World’s End, before it is obscured by cloud (5am btw, so we did a walk to Little Adam’s Peak instead). Although we had agreed a pre-defined itinerary, Rohan was more than happy to make adjustments along the way and to take into account any specific interests we had. When we commented how much better the fruit tasted in Sri Lanka than the UK, Rohan went out his way to stop en-route to pick up whatever was local to the area through which we were travelling. For example: Yellow bananas – smaller that those in the UK, but ten times more delicious. Red bananas – even nicer than yellow bananas. Mangos – several different varieties. The big ones are particularly nice, and are enough for two. Yellow coconuts – lots of milk, and then split to eat the thin white layer. Much nicer than green… Jack fruits – never heard of these before. Had the strangest consistency and taste, but definitely recommended. A drink made from a fruit that only grows in mud flats in one area of Sri Lanka – can’t remember what it was called, but it is a must try. Cashew nuts – also sold by the side of the road. Almost creamy in flavour. Rohan proved invaluable in other ways as well: on our Jeep safari through Yala National Park, he spotted a Leopard in a tree - something no-one else in the vehicle (including the driver) had spotted. We had several minutes watching the Leopard, before it decided to climb down – as the most anyone else saw that day was a tail disappearing into the scrub, I am grateful for Rohan’s keen eyesight. Sadly, since the bombing earlier this year, tourists numbers are down 80% - this means Sri Lanka is currently a real bargain. You can stay in 4 and 5 star hotels, for the price of 2 or 3 star. Finally, I will say Sri Lanka is a must visit - the people are happy and friendly, and it is clean (I think even less litter that the UK). The wildlife is plentiful, even outside the wildlife parks - this is probably helped by the predominantly Buddhist culture, and the fact that farmers are compensated for any damage done by elephants. Give Sri Lanka and Danulanka Tours a go – you will not be disappointed.

review_text: We came here with two kids ages 10 and 13. We are frequent hikers so this was a supremely easy hike. What we liked: - easy hike, takes less than an hour - the start of the trail begins through tea-farms and beautiful bungalows looking out at Ella Rock. - the views of the valley and mountains are really nice. review_text: #Little #Adams #Peak #Hiking Ella is a hiking hotspot in the mountain country of Sri Lanka. Some of the views from hikes in Ella are phenomenal with the region well known for its tea plantations and spectacular mountain ranges. If you want to enjoy some of the best views without needing to hike for hours, Little Adam’s Peak is the perfect trek, especially for an unforgettable sunset. It’s one of the top things to do in Sri Lanka if you enjoy hiking! The trail begins with a moderate incline as it winds through tea plantations. It will lead you up to 1141m above sea-level although you already begin at a high elevation so you will only hike up a few hundred meters. The trail is marked the whole way with well-maintained paths and stairs to the first set of viewpoints. There are multiple platforms, rocks, and viewpoints perfect for photos once you hit the top of Little Adam’s Peak. Although, you can and should keep going along the ridge and the view only gets better. As you continue along the ridge the trail gets a little wilder and you might get a little dirty, managing your way up and down to the final viewpoint. We hung out at the top of Little Adam’s Peak with no one else around, taking in the mountains and the epic scenery of the 360-degree views. We probably waited a little too long to head back and ended up trekking back down in the dark. For just a short hike, Little Adam’s Peak gives you unbelievable views and is the ideal way to spend sunset in Ella. Stay safe and enjoy! We warmly welcome you to Sri Lanka.. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Climbing Little Adams peak was one of the activities our tour guide had organised for us whilst in Ella. Setting off early in the morning to avoid the heat we assume, it is a fairly steady walk along for a while, then a climb up some steps to the top. You do not need to be an Olympic athlete to climb this, but a certain level of fitness is required, and the last bit is quite steep; those used to walking and hiking should find it a breeze. The whole climb up and back took approx. 2 hours, but you will definitely work up a sweat doing so !  I would strongly recommend sensible footwear e.g. trainers or walking shoes, and some water ! On the way up we passed some tea pickers in the fields next to the path, who were more than happy to pose for some pictures, for a small reward / LKR tip of course ! Once at the top there is another good photo opportunity stood next to the small statue / shrine, and then some absolutely stunning views over the surrounding countryside and the valley below. There is a large rock ledge where everyone takes their turn to stand on or dangle their legs over the edge and take photos. On the way back down we passed the tea pickers again, who were now having some food - probably lunch since they start so early in the morning ?  There was also a little coconut / drinks shack hut that had opened up on the way down, where you can buy a well deserved cold drink to cool down with. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam’s Peak is a fairly easy hike found in Ella, Sri Lanka and is a short 20-minute walk from the center of town. Also, it’s completely FREE! The entrance is easily located on Google maps, but just in case, you can find the entrance between The Chillout Ella and the Ella Flower Garden Resort. The hike starts with a very slow ascent through a dirt path surrounded by tea fields and stunning views of the lush green valleys that shroud hill country. You’ll make your way along said path for about 15-minutes depending on your walking speed where you’ll see the staircase that leads all the way to the peak; you literally cannot miss it!   The best time to climb Little Adam’s Peak would be sunrise. There aren’t many early risers, therefore you will beat the crowds if you go for sunrise. Little Adam’s Peak has a great effort to view ratio which is why tourists flock here all year round to catch glimpses of the beautiful tea country laid out below.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Among the attractions in Sri Lanka, Little Adam's Peak impressed me most with her natural rustic setting, breathtaking mountainous scenery and memorable hike. I was born and brought up in a metropolis city bombarded with irritating noise from the zooming vehicles and factory machineries; the atmosphere pervaded with toxic pollutants from the car exhausts and industrial chimneys. But here in Ella and the Little Adam's Peak, the setting was so different with lush greenery everywhere and very far from the madding crowd. As I slowly wandered among the lush greenery, the lyrics of the Happy Wanderer resonates in my ear: I like to go a wandering up the mountain track. And as I go, I love to sing My knapsack on my back. Val-deri, val-dera. Val-deri, val-dera Ha, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha Ha Val-dera. My knapsack on my back Another thing wonderful about Ella is that the nearby attractions, be it this Little Adam's Peak, the Nine Arch Bridge, the waterfall are all within walking distance from the train station and near the town center. The hike to Little Adam's Peak was comfortably done without I even realized that I was at the summit of the mountain. It was something slightly more difficult than climbing Bukit Timah Hill in Singapore. Early morning at about 6.30 am, I strolled my way from my hostel to the town center. The road to the Little Adam's Peak is on the left turn from the town center. I had my simple breakfast of a plate of two pieces of coconut roti with a cup of Ceylonese tea in one of the restaurants along the road to the scenic attraction. There was a morning bazaar on the street just at the junction of the town center and the adjoining road to the Little Adam's Peak. I enjoyed seeing the locals in their daily morning routine. It took me about half an hour to arrive at the base of the Little Adam's Peak. The lush greenery of the tea plantations that followed and the rustic setting of the village and the hillside track really uplifted my hiking spirit. The magnificent looming Ella Rock mountain appeared robustly gorgeous and was a beautiful sight as we hike up the track to the summit. It was a uphill laborious climb though it was not that high. I was panting heavily as the steps were steep but the moment I reached the summit, the panoramic mountainous view was spectacularly impressive and gorgeous. Breathtaking views and a rustic scenery. The air is fresh, the environment calm and peaceful and the scenery beautiful. It is waste if you miss this when you are in Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The other reviews talk about the stairs, zip line, etc. The walk up is not difficult, there are beautiful breezes, views, scenery.  It’s lovely and we recommend going. At the top of the first peak you come to (the ice cream man is likely there), there are some stray dogs that definitely depend on tourists to survive. We brought a large tin bowl and filled it with water.  We also brought a lot of dry dog food.  Please bring something for these precious, sweet dogs when you go. You can refill the bowl with water and bring food. Also, the ice cream that the man there is selling is really good.  A lot of people were buying ice cream cones (he filled each cone with vanilla ice cream).  We had a cone each. Parents were buying for kids and themselves. We also bought two cones for the dog that apparently had puppies.  (Not sure where the puppies were. Hopefully someone rescued them.) We held the cones while she licked the ice cream. So, Little Adam’s Peak, including the walk through town to get there, is so nice and we recommend it.  But please remember to think of the dogs and help them. 🧡

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adams Peak is a great short trail walk that is very well sign posted and easy to get to. The walk up and down is approximately 40 minutes return however I would allow at least 30 minutes at the top because the view is spectacular (sunrise and sunset are best). Most of the walk is flat however the last 10 minutes up is steep with a lot of stairs. I would recommend wearing enclosed shoes. There are approximately 10 dogs that live at the top of the peak, 5 of which are very small puppies. There is a water bowl at the top for them, so I highly recommend taking a water bottle to fill up their bowl for them. We also purchased some Pedigree dog biscuits from Ella Gap Supermarket in town which all the dogs at the top loved. They are reliant on humans for food and water due to living up there. All of the dogs are friendly and it’s definitely a must do walk to the top of you’re visiting Ella!

This part was slightly more challenging but no one rushes you so take your time and catch your breath and it should be ok for able bodied people with an average fitness level. The views when you reach the top are breathtaking. Completely worth the hundreds of steps. Absolutely stunning. We left our hotel in Ella by foot about 8.30am to avoid the hot sun. It took about 1.5 hrs to get to the top, chill and take pics and then get back down. Bring plenty of water with you. We also teamed this walk with a walk ro 9 arch bridge as it's close by. My highlight of Ella for sure

Take the one from the left side (which shows direction towards the villas). And after a while take the right. This will help avoid climbing around 50 steps in the end. Its not a very tough climb after that. The views are excellent. Just too good. This one cannot be missed!! At sunset the views keep getting better. You can spend roughly 2-3 hrs here. Beautiful place without any entry fee!!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It took 1 hour us to climb up. Worth going there because we were able to capture so much of nice landscaping pictures. Make sure you have good shoes to protect your toes and fingers as it is little bit slippery way and Also make sure to bring a water bottle.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We went on Saturday and it was very crowded with local and international tourists. There were some women posing as tea pickers and asking money for photographs, some of them having a small child with her. Once you get on the top, walk little further from the first hilltop - it's takes a bit of climbing, but you get stunning views with almost no people around. Strangely, there are a lot of dogs and puppies.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: With my wife and 2 kids went on a short trek ti Little Adam’s Peak. The trail is easy, only when you came to the stairs it may be little challenging for completely unprepared person. Reaching the summit is rewarding as it gives you nice views of the surroundings. Plus, you do something for yourself.

review_text: An easy evening stroll up to the peak for sunset was nice and I wouldn’t go any further than describing it as a stroll, it’s definitely not Strava worthy. If you’ve got limited time in Ella and don’t fancy smashing everything in one day then this should take the hit. Pretty boring.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk from Ella to the start is a bit miserable (our driver took us but I wouldn’t have fancied a dusty hot 20 minutes at the beginning and end of an otherwise lovely walk) but once true path leaves the Road you are quickly amongst tea plantations and under trees with amazing views around each turn, the walk is fairly easy and took us about 35 minutes not rushing. There are steps at one point which aren’t as nice as the main path but are quicker if that’s what you want. Once at the top there are several viewpoints so allow an hour to wander between them all.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Lovely walk to the top of the peak through a tea plantation area where you can see tea pickers at work. If you take their photos they do expect some small payment, but when you realise how little they earn, this seems reasonable enough. The steps to the peak are quite stiff if you’re not that fit, but do-able if you go at your own pace. As ever, the reward is an amazing view. Well worth doing.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A must whilst in Ella, this is a great and easy trek through the tea plantations before arriving at the summit with sweaping views across Ella and the surrounding area. Don’t be afraid to pay the tea pickers 50-100 LKR to take some stunning photos along the way!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: 3 of us late 60s did the walk to the top of Little Adams peak, we took our time and from Ella it took approx 1.hr it is a gentle walk until you encounter the concrete steps which are steep, however once you get to the summit the views are outstanding. Unfortunately it's the same way down so you are encountering people coming in the opposite direction and have to give way as the paths near the summit are narrow. We'll worth the walk

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Well signposted route up to Little Adams Peak. Starts with a stroll through the tea plantations. Be mindful of the workers who want you to pay to take their photo (I just didn't want to take their photo!) Steps take you up the last part of the route which are an easy enough climb. Great views of the valley and over to Ella Rock from the top

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We accessed the peak from 98 Acres hotel on whose grounds the peak is situated.  This meant we arrived away from the crowds and more touristy entrance.  The hotel grounds are spectacular too.  The peak itself was very crowded when we arrived so we walked much further down where it was quieter and the views of Ella rock and the surrounding area even more beautiful.  This area is less accessible and I would only recommend it if you are wearing stout footwear and have a head for heights.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk to the summits ( first one then second one further on) is for the most part a stroll along a well trodden path. Only when you arrive at the zip line centre do you have to exert effort to ascend well made concrete steps for about 20 minutes. Be sure to have at least 2 litres of water with you. The views from the summits may cause you to want to pause, sit down and take it all in and hopefully create an indelible memory that will cause you to smile when you return home to a less exotic part of the world. 😊

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a very straightforward walk with concrete steps for the bulk of the way. The access is via the 98 Acres Resort on the edge of Ella and, once there, you simply follow the signs. From the peak there is a great ridge walk across 2 or 3 further peaks and this becomes a bit more exacting. The path here is poor underfoot, steep in places and slippy. Good footwear is essential. However if you choose to head right to the end you have even better views and a lot fewer people around.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: If you are in Ella, this is an easy walk with a big reward. We took about 90 minutes to do both ways, although it was quite busy at the top. The garden cafe at the bottom does great cappuccino and banana milk shakes, but the service is slow.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy walk not too far from the center. If you walk all the way probably 60 minutes to get there. We took a tuctuc for the first part up to the place where there can take you for 500 LKR with the three of us. Then you only walk for about 20-30 minutes to get up the first of the three hills. Easy walk to the second hill just a couple of minutes and maybe additional 10 minutes to get to the third hill as there is a steep descent and climb (and back again). There is a zip-line along the way for 20 USD pp if you fancy little additional fun on your way back (open till 5pm only, get tickets on your way up). We did not take it as we went to see the sun set and by that time they were closed already. Definitely recommend for everyone (as opposed to Ella Rock which definitely is much harder and a bit higher - see separate reviews for Ella Rock.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk (there and back) takes up to 2 hours if you climb all 3 peaks. Sensible walkers start early to avoid both the heat and the crowds - we started a little later! The first part of the walk is through attractive tea plantations, following that Sri Lanka's biggest, fastest, highest etc zip wire ride comes into view (30 dollars from memory). The busy climb continues with magnificent views all around. The sense of achievement at reaching the peaks is somewhat tempered when you see others who have also made it in bare feet, carrying babies etc! On the way down you can get your photo taken with a local tea planter - but don't forget to tip her! After 2 hours of moderate exhaustion and heat we stopped at the first bar we saw (we were actually staying overnight there) and had the most wonderful juice drink I have ever enjoyed (the venue is called Chill Out).

Probably less people there than later in the day as well. The climb is not to tough and the walk from Ella is about 45-60 minutes, a must-go-to when visiting Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My wife and I (both 27) absolutely loved this mini mountain just outside of Ella. We are keen hikers and it took about 30mins from the centre of Ella. The entire path is man made with proper steps so all abilities can do this. The path is clearly marked and it was very easy to follow it right to the top. At the top the views were amazing both of Ella rock and Ella valley. We honestly much preferred this to the actual Adams Peak!! If you leave early before the heat of the day then it is a very pleasant climb, with far fewer tourists and the views are amazing. And the best part is that it is totally free!! We really recommend this to everyone visiting Ella.

review_text: Grateful to get some amazing views after only doing half an hour or so walking up a very easy track. Lots of people saying it gets tougher nearer the top, but it just turns into steps. It’s all easy, just hot! Fortunate to see puppies curled up in a grassy bed at the top too. The views all around are really great!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Worth the climb! I would advise to go early because of the heat. You start off with a stroll past tea fields. Always nice.  You can climb 3 different peaks, so it's up to you whether you want to make it a big climb or not. Last one is definitely the hardest to climb, but everything is worth the view! The views are amazing.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This walk is well established and easier to follow than Ella rock, once on the start of this walk you wanted get lost. Beautiful scenery walking along the path and their are tea plantations either side with ladies going about their work. Fair few steps but doesn’t take long to get up to the top

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Definitely worth the trek the views are beautiful! I don't know what these people are talking about calling it a easy 'stroll' it is a hike up rocks with a steep incline. There are a few peaks and each one will leave you breathless. I consider myself quite fit and would not call it easy but it is very doable and like I said definitely worth it.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The "hike" to little Adams peak is apiece of cake compared to others in Sri Lanka. If I can do it hungover, you can do it on your worst day and still make it pretty easily. Once at the top the views are spectacular but please don't risk permanent injury or death for the sake of Instagram like we saw many people doing. Just enjoy the breathtaking natural beauty of Sri Lanka's hill country and walk back down. On the way there is also a zipline ($20 USD) which my wife did and found to be very enjoyable. I am too big for the zipline, so that just shows you how easy the peak is to climb. If my tubby butt can do it, so can you, and you'll be rewarded with the views from the top. Have fun, and stay safe!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I would be hesitant to call this a hike. More like a stroll with a wee incline and at the end a few steps. Views were nice, not as nice though as from Ella Rock. In total needed about 45 minutes for up and down. A nice to do if you are in  the area.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Just a short walk out of the center of Ella, once you go through the official entry pathways you may come across people who offer to take photos for money, which is only fair as they are dressed up in traditional clothing and this is their source of income. It’s not very expensive (maybe 100 rp). Once you hit the steps it is a steep climb, which I recommend to do slowly to avoid altitude dizziness. There are two parts to the peak and you can choose to go further and climb down then up the second half of the peak which again is well worth it. They do sell water at the base but it is a tough walk so make sure you stock up on water before you ascend.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is obviously busy, but it's not really very far or difficult, so allow maybe  90 mins up and back, then have lunch or a drink at the hotel/cafe at the rod which also seems to sell plants. We actually saw some interesting birds on this walk despite the  number of people

review_text: The views that you get at the top are amazing. Only took around 2/3 hours to go up and come back down. Not a difficult walk first through the tea fields and then up the peak not bad and not strenuous although frequent rest stops may required for the less fit. Take water in a permanent water bottle, disposable plastic is not allowed

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked to 9 arch bridge then across to Little Adams Peak. An easy enough walk up but on our way down we took a wrong turn, got lost for a while and found ourselves in a small village where the tea pickets live, which was an interesting dectour, then the heavens opened but we were prepared. All in All a good experience with fantastic views from the top. Highly recommend you do this walk

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We travelled with 7 young kids (ages 2-13).  We did the 2 year old in a backpack and the 4 year old and up walked their own way.  Nice little walk, very nice views.  The trail is a little crowded and of course it’s a but touristy but for young families we enjoyed. There is a sweet looking zip line for $20 usd (adults) $15 usd kids (under 15, but need to weigh 30 kgs).  We didn’t do it but looked worth it and pretty sweet. After Littles Adam’s just a quick walk to 9 arch bridge.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk up Little Adams Peak is a great way to kick off your hiking in Ella.  It's a straight forward walk that only gets a bit challenging at the end when it gets a little steeper.  The view from the top is well worth it.  You may want to head up early or late, as because it is a shortish walk, through the middle of the day it is rush hour traveler and can be quite congested.   The start of the track takes you through Tea Plantations and on the way back you can drop into 98 Acre Hotel and Spa, which has a public Restaurant and Bar for a few beers to admire the your earlier endeavor.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's peak is quite accessible - only about 45 minutes from the road to the top. Some parts of the walk are a little challenging if you go to the far peak but no problem for anyone reasonably mobile and with good footwear. The view is a fantastic panoramic vista of the valleys and surrounding hills.

review_text: It was quite a challenging walk /climb and took us over an hour to get to the top - but then we’re not young or particularly fit! It was well worth it, fantastic views going up, walking amongst the tea pickers and then amazing views from the top! They’re just about to open a zip wire at the end of the month at $29 a pop - it looked great fun but locals said they wouldn’t be the first to try it!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This walk  is very  quite, shaded and easy, except the last part where there are about one hundred steps. Going up, one passes near a tea workers village, with a nice small  temple and very poor dwellings. At the top, one enjoyes a wide vew of the hills.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Not far from the main high street, the route up to the summit is not difficult but you need to take water with you. It takes approximately a hour to send your way up the hill taking in the view of the surrounding hills as you go. Plenty of photo opportunities and on reaching the top the views are spectacular. To reach the farthest point you need to walk the saddle back where further sights can be enjoyed. For those of you unable to walk, the journey can be partly made by tuk tuk or even scooter.  The top however is inaccessible by these. An interesting site halfway up was the start of a cable car construction. A useful addition for the less adventurous when completed.

review_text: If you walk from the Main Street in Ella, you’re talking about a 30 minute walk to the incline part and say another 15-20 minutes of steep hills and steps. I wouldn’t call this hike challenging, saw some young children and older adults in their 60s near the top. To be fair, the older adults were working hard. Views at the top were incredible, well worth the effort.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The road/track to the start of the peak is a well travelled path with many walkers. To the bottom of the actual peak is fairly easy going but once you get to the base of the peak then be prepared for a fairly steep climb if you want to take in the view from the very top. The views on the way up to the base are just as exciting and yes you can get the TukTuk ride up to the base but the walk gives you the chance to see the stunning views as well as some local living areas.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The way to Little Adams Peak is not very well marked. We walked some distance past it.  Once we found it we hiked up to the top. In a few months time there will be a cable car, but it looks like it will only go up to the base. The stairs up are a bit haphazard, with varying heights, but it is still worth going up to the top for the view.  Some Korean tourists in our hotel went up to see the sunrise....not sure how they went because we didn’t see any evidence of lighting on our way up!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I went twice to see the sunrise at the little adam’s peak because it was absolutely breathtaking! It’s a very easy hike up there, everybody can do it but you should still wear good shoes because the last part is a bit difficult with flip flops (and it’s pretty cold there in the morning so bring a warm sweater and long trousers!).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Nice walk to the top and you are rewarded with a nice view of the mountains and valleys around. Can be hot on a sunny day! May be a little difficult and tiring for little children, but they can stop before it gets steep up the steps.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We did Nine Arch Bridge first then Little Adam's Peak. There are stairs first to go up the peak, I thought ohh stairs that's easy, but no. Stairs first then after it becomes harder. I was wearing a long white skirt, carrying a handbag and in elevated sneakers. I did not come prepared :) There are 3 peaks, don't be happy when you made it up the first one, it's not over yet. The first peak was very easy, once we made it there we saw Peak 2. It looks easy from where we stand but it's definitely not once you start making your way down the path. It was very windy, I felt abit dizzy and off balance like I am going to fall off, I am not a fan of heights. I did a lot of bending down (putting one foot down first then the other) and holding the ground/rocks for balance, it helped a lot. Then after you need to climb up to the peak 2. Again holding on to rocks and ground. Its like up down up down kinda climb. Once we were up there the view is breathaking but it didn't look very nice in the pictures. There are other people doing the climb, there will be a time/spot that you need to let the other person go first and you need to becareful to hold your position and not slip. After enjoying the view we decided not to proceed to peak 3 and made our way back and again it's down up down up down climb. We wanted to wait for the sunset but we saw thick clouds and assumed that we will not be able to see any sunset and it will get dark soon better to make our way down while theres still light. Once we arrived back in Ella city we saw the sunset but from below, OOOPS! I am pretty impressed with myself; wearing a long white skirt, carrying a handbag and in elevated sneakers and I made it to the top. Instead of laughing at myself for being unprepared I would prefer to just say hey I did it with all of that, If I can do it, I am sure you can do it too (of course I don't mean you have to dress up like me, I just mean as in I'm not a very sporty person so if I can make the climb so can you).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a good hike to do if you arrive in Ella too late to start the Ella Rock hike but want to hit the trails anyway!  It's a short walk along Passara Road, then turn right at Ella Flower Garden Resort and follow the trail to the top.  It'll be busy, but it's quite a nice walk through the tea plantations, and while there are steep steps further up, pretty much anyone should be able to do it!  The view from the top, over towards Ella Rock, is nice!  There's also another additional section to an alternative viewing point further on - this is a little bit more technical so I'd only recommend this if you've got a decent pair of shoes on (I saw way too many folks slipping and sliding over the rocks in their gripless footwear!).  You can also couple this hike with the 9 Arch Bridge by carrying along Passara Road and dropping down to the bridge - come back via the railway line for a nice 10km or so circular.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This was one of my favorite things that we did in Ella. If we were staying longer, I would have done it again! We went up around 9AM, and it was starting to get crowded. It was an easy hike to the first peak, but if you go further it gets a little steeper. I would definitely recommend to wear athletic shoes if you plan on doing that. I saw a lot of people coming back holding their sandals in their hands. Once we reached the first view point, we went to the next peak, which was still a bit crowded. We went on to another one and there was hardly anyone there! So it was nice to sit there in the quiet and enjoy the views. The trails are marked really well, so it was not hard to find. If you are going to be in Ella, I highly recommend doing this short hike!

review_text: We really enjoyed our climb to the summit of Little Adam's Peak. Once leaving the Passara road there is a well surfaced path which gently climbs the hillside above the tea plantations. After a 10-15 minute gentle walk there was a sign to the right for mini Adam's Peak. After a short walk on a stone path there are well maintained concrete steps which lead you up most of the short, steep climb to the summit. This would take no more than 10 minutes with breather breaks. When the steps finish there is a short climb (10-15m) on rough paths, basically just pick one you like the look of and climb up it! And then you are at the summit, where we were rewarded with fabulous views as fortunately it was a clear day when we walked, failing the view there are a couple of nice Buddha statues! The route back down retraces your steps. You could, as we did, when you get back to the sign for mini Adam's Peak turn right to stop off at Cafe 98 (at 98 Acres resort) and extend the walk by heading over to 9 arches bridge and along the railway line back into Ella.

review_text: The views from Little Adam’s Peak are spectacular. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We almost didn’t come here because a traveller we met said how treacherous part of the walk was - what nonsense! This was a delightful, straightforward walk that can be done in an hour and a half or from beginning to end and back again. We were staying in Ella main town, and from there we just walked down Passara Rd until we saw the trail for Little Adam’s Peak begin. No need to take a tuk-tuk, the the walk is only 10 minutes to the start, if that. The walk itself was very pleasant, starts off very easy, just a mild elevation as you walk through tea plantations, then gets steeper as you walk up the hill. There are parts which are quite rocky and you do need to walk carefully so I’d recommend wearing trainers rather than sandals. That being said, people of all shapes and sizes were managing it, including families with small children. The views themselves were lovely. You can see far across Ella, and it’s a great way to soak in all the tea plantations around you. Overall, in terms of how straightforward the walk was and the views you get from doing it, I’d give this a full 5 stars and recommend that anyone visiting Ella come and do this walk.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The view is just incredible. Its just acres of lush greenery everywhere you look other than the main road that you see winding around in the distance. The hike isn't difficult at all even with kids since the trail has been well traveled on.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: After about a 2 km walk from the Ella town we came to the start of the track to Little Adam’s Peak. It was a rainy day so The climb up started with a muddy road in the middle of a tea estate after which a steep climb of steps to the top. The climb of course was a bit slippery cuz of the rain but the view up was worth the climb. Unfortunately we couldn’t catch the sunset cuz of the gloomy weather but nevertheless the breeze and the mist and the surrounding made up for it.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It takes a couple of hours from Ella - you can cut it down by taking a tuktuk and then the stairs - but we thought we’d embrace the views so we took the trail up. Start early as it gets hot, so we left about 0730. During the winding trail, we ran into a “tea lady” who posed for photos and pointed us off in a path that didn’t look all too like a trail. I’d read on here they can send you in wrong directions etc. So I was wary but stuck with it - it was a challenging route she sent us but we made it up in one piece. The top, while very busy with tourists, has fantastic views. A must see.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We visited Ella in August and found it to be one of the most scenic places ever. We walked from our accommodation to Little Adam's Peak using just the printed town map dished out by the Tourist stand. It is very straightforward and well signposted from the main road. The walk takes in stunning views at every angle, and shows off Sri Lanka at her most beautiful best. There was also a snake charmer sat around one corner, but we didn't stop for the show. We walked up in trainers, but locals were ascending and descending in flip flops, so it's not a difficult walk - would note that we did it in dry weather - but do take water as it can be a hot one.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Two friends, my wife, little son and I climbed Little Adam's Peak in August. The hike is not very challenging (I was carrying our son and my wife our backpack), but totally worth the effort. After reaching the top, the view across Ella and the surrounding area (e.g. Ella Rock) is brilliant and somehow it's not too crowded (there are also multiple different view points) so that you can definitely enjoy the atmosphere. Furthermore we don't think that a guide is necessary for the hike. We did it on our own using free navigation apps. From our perspective Little Adam's Peak is definitely a must see and we'll come back for sure on our next trip to Ella.

review_text: We set off around 9am when it was already quite warm. There were people of all ages, nations and fitness levels on the walk in both directions. The route is quite obvious and most of the climbing is gradual. There were heaps of people on the summit when we arrived so we took a left turn and traversed across to Little Sri Padaya to the south-east - this route is steep and more strenuous: don't do it if you're not fit. Great to sit quietly and enjoy the view, including Ella Peak across the valley and Ravana Falls / Ella Gap. After a quick visit to the summit and shrine we detoured coming back to visit the Green Tea Factory, which was closed🤔 Set off early if you don't like the heat.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Travel in Ella was truly beautiful journey including the landscape and nature are amazing, and one of the highest reason is to climb Little Adam's Peak. 1) Little Adam’s Peak is 1141m high. So please refer to the tittle of "little", means it's not Adam's Peak. Both was located in different district. 2) From the main road in Ella town, u need to walk about 3km-4km to find the main entrance for start the trail. Means u will see the signage of Little Adam's Peak. 3) From main entrance, the trail begins with a moderate incline as it winds through tea plantations around 10-15minutes. 4) After the tea plantations, u need to follow the steps of stairs trail. I don't know exactly how many steps it's, may be around 300++ stairs. It's will take 20-30minutes to go up depend on your stamina. 5) The stairs trail is well-maintained and u can see the spectacular view but beware because the steps are not the same height. 6) Please wear comfortable and sturdy shoes on your way up. Bring mineral water. Use sunblock/sunscreen, hat or anything u think needed. 7) Little Adam's Peak was easy for hikers and moderate trail for others. But u will not regret about that because on the top u can see 360 view of mountain (including Ella Rock). 8) Just for info that, taxi/auto also bus is available there, from the main road to the entrance.

review_text: After conquering Ella rock the day before Little Adam was a breeze. We went to nine arch bridge first and followed maps.me on the way back to find the hidden footpaths which lead to Little Adams Peak, a lovely flat walk until you get to it and some steep steps to reach the top. We saw a lot of families with small children so a nice “hike” to do with little ones. Definitely worth it to see the views.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Great little hike with kids. We got totally drenched by rain, and I swear it wasn't raining anywhere else in Ella. Bring an umbrella or rain coat.  But amazing views, though we nearly didn't noticed because of the pouring down rain. Must do in Ella.

review_text: Much as we huffed.and puffed and moaned (part of the fun), we would not have missed this fantastic walk with a good path (mainly steps) for the sheer pleasure if doing it and the lovely views.  Lots of camaraderie wirh other mini hikers. We combined this on a visit to tea factory, walked down thr country lane to Ella Station, walked along track to 9 Arch Bridge then onto main road and took tuk tuk to 98 Acres and started there - in fact we could have just walked a little down the road and started there. Its marked on local tourist map

review_text: It took around 4 hours to climb up and come down. It has  beautiful view. We also checked into 98 acres resort and spa, to refresh our selves. Tip: If the view is covered from the mist, don't leave. Wait until it get clears. You will never regret the time you waited.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Just so we all know, there are 2 parts to the Little Adam’s Peak “walk”. The first part is medium and gets quite steep towards the end. I wouldn’t say it was “easy”. So you know, I’m about 157cm and 55kgs so average weight and fitness. The second part of the walk is literally climbing rocks. You have to traverse to a second mountain top. It descends at like 1.5m every horizontal meter in some parts and you have to use your arms. This was not for some of the members of my group. In any case, I loved the views once at the top and the challenge was absolutely worth it!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: In the summer of 2018 we (Dutch familie of 4, kids 13 and 18) travelled to discover the beauties of Sri Lanka. We climbed up (and were not alone) and had a great view when we arrived at the top (easy on slippers, but we had our hiking boots on). We went on a little further on the peak and were glad we had our big boots on then! On the way down some Tamil women tried do get photographed for money. We continued our walks down to the nine arches railway bridge.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adams Peak is in Ella Passara/Namunukulla road and just 1.5 km away from the Ella City centre. From Flower Garden Restaurant have to walk up to the top of the mountain.  There are few steps and through the plantation have to proceed. One could enjoy the spelindid view of the southern province.  If any traveller needs the eye catching sun rise view have to be on top of the mountain by atleast 6 am. Similar way in the evenning  sun set view by arround 6 pm. Only one request from the writer is that do not throw away the plastic bottles or any other disposable items.  Please bring them back to keep the place clean for the next traveller to enjoy the site on clean environment. A. Rozario

review_text: It's a easier hike which will take half and hour. View is beyond imagination.360° panorama view can be seen by different view points. If you want you can go for a hike to adjoining small mountains which are part of Mini Adams peak. You can see famous 98 Acres Resort from there with picturesque view.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Lovely walk with great views across the valley and to Ella rock. The path is easy and anyone can do it. There are a lot of steps towards the top so if your knees are not to o good just take it slowly. You can return to Ella via 9 arch bridge.Retrace your path to the entrance to the park then turn right and follow the road. After 30 mins or so there is a sign to the bridge. There are locals who are happy to point the way. At the bridge you can walk back to Ella thru the tunnel and along the train track there are also tuk tuk you can hire.. we walked back along the road which was a nice walk but easy to take the wrong turn.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Do this walk early. We set of at 7am and we’re at the top by 0740. It’s a fairly easy walk from Ella less the last 500m which is up some fairly unrelenting steps. Once you’re on the top all effort of getting there are quickly forgotten. We were there pretty much on our own and your rewarded with stunning 360 degree views. Beautiful pre breakfast walk.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We really enjoyed the short but tough hike up from Ella town to Little Adam's Peak for stunning views of the surrounding countryside. It was a very, very hot day on our ascent which made it tougher so bring plenty of water and a hat. The walk starts off as a steep broken stone path that eventually turns into steep steps and, as you get closer to the peak, a dirt trail. Take your time and it's not a particularly hard climb. The altitude makes you a little short of breath but with a steady rhythm or plenty of short breaks it will take you maybe 30 or 40 minutes depending on your fitness. It took us 25 minutes bit other told us they were climbing for twice that. At the top there are three or four viewing points along the ridged peak. It makes for great photos. Beautiful fresh air and scenery.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We stayed at misty view homestay which was not too far from the start of the walk so decided to go straight after we checked in. We had been told that it was easy to do without a guide so started walking with a little map of Ella which told us when to turn off for Little Adams peak. Once on the path it is super easy to follow and there are plenty of people to follow if you are unsure. It was a nice relaxing walk through tea plantations until you reach the steps which are a bit steeper. It doesn't take long to get up the steps and the views on both sides were lovely! The whole trip doesn't take long and isn't very taxing. We walked over to the 9 arch bridge after.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's peak is a range of mountain forms one side of Ella gap. You can reach there by Ella-Passara road in one kilometer. It is a short hike but beautiful view.This mountain range provides a bird’s eye view towards southern and eastern plains. You don't need a guide to hike it.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Would opt for 3.5 stars if an option, but for such a well known attraction, this is a low key, rather scruffy climb. The  view is good but not quite as good as from the cafe at 98 acres, buildings/structures are a bit dilapidated and the path is eroding fast. If you feel up to the scramble, there is a more challenging extension - in the shape of three further peaks along the ridge. Both more interesting and much less crowded these are worth the effort.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy walk most the way and then up some steep stairs to the top. Well worth the journey and far easier than Ella’s rock! Follow Pasara Road our of town, when you hit Ella Garden Resort there is a path next to ‘Chill out’ hostel that takes you up to the top. We came a different route down to see Nine Arches Bridge. Walk through 98 Acres resort and just after the main reception buildings are stone steps down to the road. Turn left on the road until you reach a few stalls and Hindu temple. Take the path down past the temple, at the edge of the lake take the path down and follow round. becomes quite steep!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The 30 minutes or so easy hike up was pleasant. We got to see some tea plantations and an impressive termite mound in the way up. The view at the top was nice although parts were a bit covered in mist. I recommend to start the hike up from Ella at about 4:45 pm and wait to watch the sunset that occurs around 6 pm. The hike is suitable for kids.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a great walk that's not too difficult. There were lots of children doing it with their families and it doesn't take too long - from the entrance to the footpath, it only takes about 30-45mins to get to the top. There's an unmistakable track all the way (I've attached a useful map I found online to help find the start of the track), but it's the stairs as you near the top that are the killer! I started up just after 9 - there were already some people coming down and it was already starting to get hot. There's a right turn just before you enter into the 98 Resort spa area that is labelled 'Mini Adam's Peak' - there were a number of tuk tuk drivers there telling people to turn. It was quite quiet when I reached the top - it started to get much busier around 10.30/11 as I was leaving. Once you're at the top, you can see another peak to your left. There is a track that goes down and up again from the top - I sat and contemplated it for a little while and had decided not to do it as it's quite steep, but then saw some young children doing it and decided that if they could manage, so could I! It was more of a scramble/ climb than a walk, but easier than I'd initially expected (just hard on the knees as you're going down!). It was well worth doing, though, and I'd definitely recommend it. I spent a fair bit of time at the top just enjoying thr views before heading down and finding my way to Nine Arch Bridge.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: And so with our legs still feeling the hike up Adams Peak from two days earlier we took on this "Little" version.  It was do-able and the views were amazing.  There were tourists and their behaviour to observe.  Dogs and lizards at the top.  Short tracks across the ridge to explore and those incredibly nerve-racking times when common sense has to prevail when sheer drops are right there!  We noted on the way up the lovely place to stay that looked like it had amazing facilities and a great view of Little Adams Peak from its rooms but decided we would take the view from our property in Ella any day.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Currently staying at 98 Acres which is basically on the way up. We can clearly see the summit of little adam’s peak from our room it’s so close.  In the few days we’ve been here there is almost a constant stream of people going up and down all hours of the day. We were told to go up early to avoid the most and get the best views. Having said that I was up around 7.30 the last 2 mornings and the most had already rolled in. Having having 3 lazy teenagers in tow who hate early starts, we decided to go up towards sunset instead. Left our room at 5pm and it was an easy path and then maybe a few hundred steps up till almost the top.then the last little bit through some rocky/grassy bits to the top. Took about 15-20 mins tops from hotel and that was at a leisurely pace. Whole trip including time up there took an hour and we were back in our room. I’m terrified of heights but even I made it up there! Well worth the walk. Views at top great. You don’t need to go super early as it’s lovely whatever time you go. Got some great pics whilst the sun was starting to set. It gets dark about 7-7.15pm here at the moment. Do as long as your on your way back down by 6.30pm you’ll be fine. Bear  left at the top to get some pics on an overhanging rock that looks like your hanging off a cliff when you sat on it. Bear right and you’ll go up to see Big Adams peak and there are some Buddhist shrines and very cute puppies also at the moment!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Good first hike to get you ready for Ella Rock (but I would suggest on a different day!). From Ella, relatively flat until final climb of stairs. However, gets a lot steeper and skippering if you choose to go further along the ridge - would definitely need runners/hiking shoes. From there, can walk to the Nine Arch Bridge but be away of kids showing you the way and then asking for money (you can say no).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked along the rails from Nine Arch Bridge and we went straight to Little Adam's Peak after that. It was a very short climb, easy to make wearing what kind of footwear you desire. The view from above is wonderful, it's a must do if you are in Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We did make this mini trek on a cloudy and breezy afternoon with kids. The views from the top of the Ella Rock were great however the flight of stairs was steep - there is little room for error and one can not afford to slip. It took us about 15minutes to walk to the base of the hill and another 10minutes to get to the top. I would say one can comfortably do this with children aged 6 and above. Though a subjective matter, I’d say someone with below average fitness /stamina can pull it off. There is no store selling food or water at the base of the hill so ensure you take whatever you wish to, beforehand.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We came here as part of a circular walk through 98 acres and to Nine Arch Bridge. It’s an easy walk, there are some steps at the end but they aren’t bad if you have moderate fitness and even in the rain didn’t get very slippery. Fantastic views through the tea fields as you go, make it a worthwhile walk. It kept showering with rain when we went but we didn’t let it put us off. Much easier than Ella Rock and a must do in Ella. There are toilets at the cafe at the base of the turn off and also in 98 acres. That was a lovely place to stop for a drink and rest and shelter, and also had fabulous views.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Views are amazing and walk is not too hard. The tea fields are beautiful and the views over the valley are so lovely. It's also only a short walk from Ella and then about 40mins from the bottom up - the walk is fairly easy with a windey path and then steps and a tiny bit of scrambling. Young kids could be seen running up the steps with parents trailing behind haha! Make sure you go!!!!!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I have climb here very often with people from different countries since i am a tour guide. Whenever i climb here i just look the expression on the faces of the guests, they will be amazed with the view and i love to see people are being happier by my country. Trust me, you will never regret the 40mins walk and climb. Specially for all European girls, this is one best place for you to take amazing pics 😉
