location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Make sure you set up early (6.00 am) to visit the mountain peak. It is a very easy walk until you get to the foot of the mountain. The set of stairs will challenge those who, like me, have lapsed in their fitness regime, but it is nonetheless a very manageable feat.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A steep walk up the stairs and then a small path up the hill a couple of km and then you are rewarded with a great view over hills like Ella rock, teaplantages and more. You can get a coconut or fluids on top or bottom but bring water cause its hot.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: After reading the reviews I felt like I was prepared for Little Adams Peak. 1hour each way is with plenty of photo times, this was correct and very generous. I don’t think I was ready for the stairs but nonetheless, made it to the top enjoyed the beautiful surroundings. Easy to get to, would not say easy if you have no fitness (like myself). Worth the trip

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We came here 3 times! It is a really easy hike. Took us about 30mins to summit. The entrance is from 98 Acres resort. From there, head towards the spa and yoga area. If you on an vehicle, it will bring you right to the entrance. There will be a police post and an easy mostly stairs trail. Once on top, there is 2 other peaks you can enjoy.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A short hike with a hilly incline towards the end of the walk.  A great misty view at the top of the peak.  Pretty walking through the tea fields, the ladies were coming back from working in the plantations whilst we were walking. A great thing to do if you have a spare hour or so in Ella Wear walking shoes as the rocky incline at the end will be hard otherwise

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adams peak is fairly easy to climb and has much better views from the top. You can start the trek from the road near flower garden restaurant and go through the tea fields until you find the stairs to the top. On the way you can see the 98 acres hotel and can visit its helipad as well. There few peaks reachable from Adams peak and the final one is bit harder to climb. If you are in fairly good health you can do it. Views are awesome from top where you can see the majesty of Ella rock. When come down you can also go through the 98 hotel premises as well if you wish.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adams peek is small hike which any one who dont have much physical problem can do. The track is not much long so you and go and come down in an hour or little more time. The entire walk is very beautiful with some amazing view of vally, mountain and tree garden around. There is small Budha temple on top and some really great view of this beautiful Srilankan town elle. A must do.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Really enjoyed this walk. We did it with our 9 and 11 year old and found it to be a great walk. Left from town at 6.30am and took about 50 minutes to reach the peak. A fairly easy walk with a short section of reasonably steep steps at the end but not an issue at all for our kids. Rewarded with beautiful views all around.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The route is very easy to follow and not too difficult. Many people know the way so you can ask locals and they will happily point you in the right direction. The views from the top are very nice. There is a second 'peak' that you can go to and get a different view. It took us about an hour up and back but that was at a slow pace and taking time to enjoy the surroundings.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Set off around 8.30 am. Beautiful scenery. Not too strenuous. Well laid out path, clean and peaceful. We didn’t go to the recommended 98 acres....although that view and hotel look stunning set amongst a tea plantation. We returned to where we set off - Breeze Cafe in around 90 min with a lot of time spent with photos and views.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: So beautiful place to see the sun rice early in the morning. It will take nearly half and hour to climb the mountain through the steps. Better start climbing around 5.30am in the morning and around 6.15 the sun will start to rice. When the sun rice you can see all misty will go away and you can see the whole ella area including the ella rock in front of you.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The diminutive ‘Little’ Adam’s peaks is not actually so little after all. Although the walk only takes about an hour each way, the views at the top are breathtaking. The walk is pleasant, through tea plantations, but it gets pretty steep at the top so bring water/sensible footwear and go in the morning unless you don’t mind sweating uncontrollably. To get there, take the turning roughly opposite the curd shop (where the bus stops) in Ella and head down that road for about 15 mins. At a sharp U bend, you’ll see signs for Mini Adams peak and you can follow the signs from there. There are little stalls selling drinks and fruit all the way up. A must while visiting Ella, especially if you’re not up to/can’t be bothered to do Ella rock (the views are said to be quite comparable).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam’s Peak and Ella Rock are often compared, somewhat condescendingly, like an older and younger brother. But although this hike is less strenuous than it’s older sibling, so to speak, it’s no mean feat. The trail is easy to find and accessible. There is no fee and no guide is necessary. When you get to the top, you have the option of carrying on along a few peaks of varying difficulty. All in all, well worth it. 44 minutes each way.

review_text: Our drive took us to a hotel through which we could walk to this peak and that cut down our walking time, wow it was some climb that got the heart racing so best to do early in the day and eat breakfast afterwards. The views are fabulous and a great photo spot. Don't buy a coconut from the  guy up the top and throw away your plastic straw! Spoils the place and hurts animals.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's peak is a great hiking route if you are a first timer. The view is amazing on the way up even if it's a little exhausting. Be sure to have plenty of water with you and wear comfortable shoes. In my experience it's best to go in the early morning because it's scorching hot in the afternoon. Overall, it is a wonderful experience that everyone should have at least once. I'd definitely go there again.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We went on others recommendation to climb early in the morning (although just missed the sunrise). We set off around 5.30am. It is a gentle slope on a concrete road. This part of the walk is lovely. There’s lots of greenery and you overlook a Hindu temple too. It is well sign posted, although we walked the wrong way at one point, but there was a sign pointing to the right to bring us back again. You can get a tuk to this point, but in reality it was the best part. After around 30 minutes of walking on the gentle slope there are some very steep, uneven stairs. These are hard work! If you’re fit it’s probably fine, but we did have to keep stopping. Also, once the stairs stop, there is a scramble to the top. You can either go left or right. We thought the right hand side was quicker but was very wrong, it was very steep, no real path and felt like we were rock climbing! So so take the left side. We did this coming back and it’s very easy. There were quite a few people at the top, and the Buddha is beautiful. Downside was a group of young girls being very disrespectful to the Buddha statue and placing their phones on it etc. All in all it took us a couple of hours to go up and come down and take a lot of photos

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It is a nice walk to the peak with a perfect view 360 degree. We did it in early morning  with a nice sunrise and you can do also meditation at least we could do as nearly nobody was there. Good view to the other mountain, waterfall, tea plantation and even to the seaside which was a little in the dust. We went also to the second summit, this way is a little bit more exposed and not so easy as the little Adam‘s Peak itself. Depending on the season during the day it becomes hot and there are no trees which could provide shadow. Take a bottle water with you as usual. Afterwards you can walk to the Green Tea factory, just 500meters.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Walk through to Tea Plantation and watch the Pluckers go about their strenuous job. They have to be mountain goats to do their job on the slopes. The steps are numerous and  the whole walk is safe. Getting a bit old so had to stop a few times. There was a man with Coconuts for drinks at the first peak and that was a welcome break before we went on. Great view from the top and our view of Little Adams from our room at 98 Acres is amazing.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This was so beautiful. The getting there can be strenuous because of the heat but just push through because it’s worth it! There are two other peaks you can climb to, I did them but was nervous because of the steepness. The view is incredible and totally worth the effort. Most of the way is steps.

review_text: We climbed Adam’s peak a few days before and to be honest the effort to get up there for little reward (was cloudy and cold but was out of season so the chances were minimal) compared to the more leisurely hike up to little Adams peak was polar opposite. Little Adam’s peak is a much nicer and shorter climb going passed tea plantations and stunning views. When the steps start the hike takes on a more aggressive gradient but it’s doesn’t take that long to get to the top for the beautiful views of Ella rock and the valleys below. The rewards for the effort is much larger and treat yourself to a juice from the local shack half way down the peak. The coconut, pineapple and lime juices are great.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A wonderful trip that can be done without any climbing at all. The first stretch goes through a beautiful scenery in a tea plantage, and the last bit has a short climb on steps of rock or concrete. The view all the way is absolutely fantastic - ending on the top of Little Adam's Peak. In total it lasts 2-3 hours with no stress. This is a must-see for all people visiting Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The path is pretty clear, not too steep, and definitely worth the climb to the spectacular view. Too difficult for younger children, but 8+ should be alright. Bring plain crackers if possible to feed the friendly dogs. Three followed us halfway up, and many dogs were around the peak. We didn't feed any (didn't have food) but I'm sure they'd appreciate it. It's better to walk up when less hot, up top there's a lovely breeze. Highly recommended to visit in Ella - Once in a lifetime breathtaking view!

review_text: After doing Ella’s rock in the morning we did this in the afternoon. Far easier than Ella’s rock with good routes and easy directions from the main road. Great for the views without the excess hiking that Ella’s rock takes.

review_text: A nice walk through the tea plantations until you reach the steps, which could be difficult for the elderly or unfit. Once to the top, you can continue on further but left that to the fitter and more adventurous. Nice view all the surrounding hills and waterfalls.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This walk is very easy to navigate from Ella town and isn’t too difficult. There are some stairs to reach the peak but it’s definitely more of a leisurely walk than a hike. We did it around 8.30/9am and the views were still nice. Good to pair with the 9 arches bridge as they’re pretty close to each other.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We read that it would be best to start the hike before sunrise, but we enjoyed our breakfast a bit too much and started the journey to the top somewhere around 7.30AM. Our host provided a map which made finding the right way quite easy (basically followed the same directions posted in many reviews). We even took a little detour through some tea plantations, but a friendly local officer guided us back to the right track. Once we got to the first peak it was clear why everyone had recommended the views. It was breathtaking. After conquering the first two peaks we decided to head back. It was very hot, and on the way down towards the Nine Arches Bridge we stopped for a refreshing drink at the 98 Acres resort cafe around 10 AM.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We completed this hike in less than 30 minutes.  It is up an easy gravel walk way, then straight up some stairs and straight back down.  Go early in the AM. It gets cloudy in the evening and you won't be cable to see anything in the afternoon! Go early.  It's maybe a 15-20 tuk tuk ride from the main part of ella.  A tuk tuk cost us about 1000-1500r to get there which included going to the nine arch bridge.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Visit for sunrise or sunset. Recommend before the midday heat. Moderate climb, well worth the effort to see the beautiful views from the peak! I went with a local guide 'Nimbal' who has great knowledge of the local area, vegetation & wildlife. Find him usually at the bus stop, or ask the locals they all know him! Ella is the BEST place to visit in Sri Lanka!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk up to Little Adam's Peak was fairly easy and doesn't take much time! When you get to the top make sure you have a camera to hand. We spent about an hour taking photos and walked further along to another great spot which required a bit of rock scrambling! Beautiful views!!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: There is Adam’s Peak, and Little Adam’s Peak. After our long day, and as evening was approaching, we elected to walk up Little Adam’s Peak. It was a nice gentle walk up the hill where you have views over the valley and its brother Adam’s Peak. On the way up, as it’s a popular tourist spot, you will meet lots of walkers. Also, you will meet lots of old women who work in the tea plantation. You may want to stop and take a picture with them, but make sure to give them a little something as they will expect it. The fog closes in fast on the mountains here, so watch and see if it’s coming in as you ascend. If it is, you may see nothing from the top but a white blanket. But this in itself is a spectacle as it closes in on the mountainside.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk to the bottom of the ascent is extremely pleasant and flat for about 20 mins. Then you get to the bottom of the Hill - 10 mins uphill steps till the top. The walk has signs so you don’t need a guide and it’s pretty easy to do. We went for sunset and when we got to the top it was so cloudy - thankfully this cleared up and we were able to see a partial sunset. Be careful though it gets dark very quickly and we ended up going back down in the dark which was pretty scary (followed by 5 dogs). The views are stunning and I would definitely recommend it for anyone visiting Ella. There’s a rock just perching off the hill and if you’re feeling adventurous it makes for a great photo!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: An enjoyable walk, mostly through tea plantations with a flat, gradual climb (so mostly easy going). The climb intensifies towards the end, with some steep stairs and a little bit of scrambling. However, nothing that anyone with a moderate fitness level (or enough time to tackle it slowly) can't handle. Views from the top of Ella Rock and surrounds are beautiful. I would suggest that you go early (or alternatively late afternoon) to avoid the heat - it is very hot up there in the sun!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Absolutely brilliant early morning hike to catch the sunrise. We had a bit of a guessing game getting to the top, but we spotted the one sign and then guessed that the stairs were the right way. The views are impressive and we spent lots of time just taking in the experience. Plenty of areas to escape the tourist and claim a corner for yourself. Good hiking shoes came in handy as we explored the 2 peeks.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We stay at ella two nights.Our lovely hotel Onrock provided us with a map and directions which was very easy to find the way to little Adams peak. Little Adams peak was a very lovely beautiful place.we climb up to the top of little Adams peak.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point

There are steps nearly all of the way - wear comfortable shoes! Also bring a raincoat as there's very little shelter if it starts raining!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam’s peak is not a difficult hike and it is really pleasant as you walk through the tea plantations and the views are splendid. The path is wide and really easy until you get to the last part which is steeper. The only thing that can make it harder is the heat of course. I really recommend walking down to the 98 acres resort for a refreshment then continuing on to the 9 arch bridge to watch the trains go by. Walking back to Ella from the bridge takes around 45 min so if you do the whole circle and take your time like I did it will take you around 4-5 hours, from the village to Little Adam’s peak, to the 9 arch bridge viewpoint then down on the bridge and railway and back to Ella station / village - this includes many stops for photos, a drink at the resort and more stops to watch the trains, otherwise I reckon you can do the whole thing in 3 hours.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It takes about an hours to climb up to a peak. You have to walk through the 98 acres resort to the entry point. Once at  the top, you can trek to few more small peaks. But only the first peak has proper steps built. Other peaks are accessible through some paths, but would not recommend on a wet day. Once at the top, you get some great views of the Ella rock and the Ella-Wellawaya road. Even the Ravana falls is visible.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We found it better than the costly tedious crowded hike in Horton Plains. Free to walk up this hill, takes about an hour to stroll up from the road. There are some steps along the way, and places you can sit if you have to catch your breath. The views are great on a clear day and its totally worth the effort.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Really nice easy walk up and great views on top! Most of the way up is a slowly inclining path with steps at the end for the first peak. Other peaks can be reached but these are a little harder. I did it in trainers and shorts and that was fine

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Just wow.  Going up to Little Adam’s peak is a fairly easy process it’s on a road off of the main road in Ella and there’s a sign pointing you in the right direction, just 2 km away.  The entrance, as others have said, is up past the Ella Flower Garden restaurant, and the path starts out paved.  Now to the good part.  The views from here a just phenomenal.  You feel like you’ve won the ticket and the breeze is just an added bonus.  There are two Buddha statues at the top, and another summit where folks like to sit on a jutted rock and take photos.  Highly recommend!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It's an easy route to climb (follow the other tourists - try not to end up at the tea plantation) and can be done in about 2 hours there and back. YOU DON'T NEED A GUIDE!! Better to go early morning when it's cooler, but bring water with you as it can get rather warm. It's about 300 physical steps and then some less pronounced sections - flat for the most part except for the steps). It's a nice view at the top and cloud doesn't tend to cover the view until the late afternoon. It's worth making it part of a bigger trip to the Nine Archway Bridge (which takes you back to Ella station) and turns the whole walk into about 4 hours. No reason not to do it while you're in town!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Ella with its wonderful landscapes was one of our favourite destinations in Sri Lanka.  Our drive from Adam’s Peak was beautiful and the village has that backpackers/independent travellers feel.  It’s possible to stay in the area for many days and have something different to do every day: trekking, visiting tea plantations, hiking to waterfalls etc.  Those restricted with time should attempt c.10km loop: Ella to Little Adam’s Peak, Tea Factory, Nine Arch railway bridge and back to Ella by following the railway tracks.  Wonderful.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak was a great relaxing walk up a winding road with tea up and down the hills on both sides and beautiful views followed by a relatively easy set of (about 250 or so?) stairs up to the top where are a couple of small Buddhas in rough shape and some different levels and views. A man was at the top selling King Coconuts and there were a number of stray dogs up top as in most places in Sri Lanka. The views are beautiful but there is little shade available so bring something to cover up if, like me, you had a bit of a pre-existing sunburn - lol. On the way down, we stopped at a stand where an absolutely lovely young woman was selling some beautiful and inexpensive handmade jewellery made from different jungle seeds. She packed the jewellery in little paper handmade pouches with written notes about what all of the seeds were from. Little Adam's Peak is also a great jumping off point to walk over to the Green Tea Factory and if you are so inclined a bit longer of a walk and scramble down to the 9 arches bridge.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Absolutely one of the most knackering treks I have undertaken - completely worth it though! We went at peak time and so was rather and busy and very hot. The stairs can be dangerous as they are very steep, I would not recommend taking young children. There is so much beauty to see on your way up, including tea pickers. If you are lucky they will let you take a photo, but do not presume as some do ask for money. The views at the top are second too none, we did not go over to the other peak as we figure the view was the same and the path looked dangerous. Take lots of water and sun cream with you. Maybe even take extra water for the poor dogs suffering in the heat, they are friendly and very grateful for water.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A must do while in Ella! First, DO NOT BRING PASTIC - Mother Nature thanks you. I recommend getting a tuktuk to the gate where the walk starts, otherwise you're just walking up a road. The first part of the hike is easy, up nicely kept stairs to the first peak, good shoes are needed but nothing fancy (I did it in flipflops). If you want to visits the 2nd and 3rd peak it gets a little more difficult as you go down one side and back up the other on a dirt "path". They do make for some great photograph opportunities!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The first half of the hike (stairs) was nice, although lots of people. The weather that day was especially hot, so the hike seemed more intense, but in fact it's a nice quick hike. If you wanna have the best view, you gotta go the extra mile. When you reach the top and look to your left, you'll see another peak with way less people. But this requires that you hike down the hill, and back up again ! ;) totally worth the effort.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We did this hike carrying an infant in a carrier and with our four-year old on foot. It is not difficult at all. There are a few steep stair bits towards the end, and the path narrows at times so you will have to wait to let people pass if it is crowded, but this is a very doable family hike. You'll be well-rewarded with beautiful views from along the ridge at the end.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This hike is very straightforward and not too long - but it all depends on your starting point. Town, or the junction on the main road, or from where the steps start ( a tuktuk can take you part of the way). There are lovely views on the way up, and from the top you can see down into the valley and across to other peaks. You can also extend your walk on other paths to a couple of other small summits. It might get a bit crowded at the top, but remember this is a straightforward walk from a fairly touristy town so of course others will be there. If you are in Ella for just one night, as I was, it's good to go up there in the late afternoon for the evening light. But come down the steps before it gets dark.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked from our hotel, guided by a map, kindly provided by them. I guess it was about 20 minutes from town to get off the metalled road and onto the tea-plantation trail. A delightful afternoon walk of about 35 mins through the tea led us to the steep ascent. This was quite taxing, but it's OK if you take it easy. Bring plenty of water. The 360-degree view is well worth the effort.

review_text: The route is easy to navigate from Ella centre head towards the Ella Gardens Guest House. The route up is a dirt track, which eventually leads to concrete steps. Do not make our mistake, when you pass the monestary/ basketball court take the left fork towards the shack. Do not carry on straight ahead as it appears on Google maps. The views of Ella Rock and the gap are stunning.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The hike to little Adam’s peak is easy and doesn’t take much time. But be aware of going to the other side of the hill because it’s quite steep and slippery. The 360 degrees view on the top is so stunning! The way to little Adam’s peak is also very pretty. Be bit careful when taking pictures of tea picker because they might ask for money. Make sure you bring sunblock because there is no shade on the top and the sun is quite strong during the day.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My advice? To get the most out of the experience, go early in the morning, around sunrise. The walk is OK, though a little tricky at the very end if you have mobility concerns. The view is breathtaking and one to savour.  If you time it, so that you return around 8am, at the bottom of the Peak, the tea pickers were fastening their sacks onto their bodies. The ladies were so friendly and charming that it made the whole experience more personal and holistic. Little Adams Peak has both a spiritual and economic significance. When attempting the climb, take water, though you can buy a coconut from the vendor at the top, so don’t panic. Give yourself around 30 mins to climb to the top, and wear good walking shoes, or trainers with plenty of grip.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My partner and I always do walks when we go away. This was an easy walk if you’re fit. If you’re slightly unfit or pregnant (like myself) there is plenty of places to stop for shade & take in the view. The last part up the stairs were the hardest but doable. When you get to the top there are 3 viewing platforms, the first 2 are majestic. My husband went to the furtherest one away (to the left). It took him 20 minutes & he is very fit. He said the views were equally amazing at the first 2 platforms. It took us around 1.5 hours to do the whole thing, we just did it at a leisurely pace. You will need some level of fitness & a water bottle & a hat/sunscreen. Worth it though.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is the shorter and easier of the two hill walks that most visitors  to Ella take. From the path that leaves the main road into Ella allow 45-55 minutes to reach the viewpoint at the top. After meandering gradually uphill through a tea plantation the  walk gets steepest over the last half mile with some 300 steps and scramble to the summit  that provides on a clear day great views down to the flat coastal belt and to the hills to the north. Be sure to carry water though half-way along the route there is an enterprising family-run juice bar selling soft  drinks and freshly-made juices.

review_text: I had climbed the more strenuous Ella Rock in the morning so i decided to climb up Little Adam's Peak in the afternoon. Unfortunately i ma over 60 and no longer so agile on my feet and found the last few meters quite dangerous and was rather nervous so i came back down immediately. The trail to the peak was very busy with locals and tourists, and appeared to be much more popular than the Ella Rock hike.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We climbed Little Adam’s Peak in really hot sunshine. The walk is easy except that it gets quite steep towards the end. Fabulous views at the top. Quite a lot of people doing the walk as well but not overcrowded as people are so friendly. A good walk and a good way to build up a thirst for a beer on a hot day!!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I’m not an early morning person but We decided to go for sunrise and I don’t regret it! We walked from our accommodation at Ella Ridge View & it was an easy walk until the final ascent which includes a steep staircase with no rail. If you aren’t a fan of stairs or need a few breaks then factor that into your allocated time to the top. But by all means don’t let a few stairs stop you because it’s an absolutely stunning view from the top.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Recommend for anyone visiting Ella. Suggest to get up early to watch the sunrise over Ella rock from Little Adams Peak. Early = beat the crowds and the heat. Sunrise is around 6.15am in March Walk takes about 2 hours for a round trip from the Main Street. Note: best wear solid footwear as there are lots of steps and some slops of rock / dust track if you want to go across to the highest point of the peak.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Set off at 9am to climb Little Adams Peak which was a perfect and civilised time, cool enough to benefit on the way up and down before the heat and intensity of the midday sun. The walk from start to finish is breathtaking with great views and wonderful photo opportunities. There is absolutely no need for a guide with a straight route up and down firstly through the tea plantations before you start to climb the steps. Yes it's hot and a little hard going at times but you can stop to rest and once you reach the top the views are amazing and you easily spend 30 minutes to an hour at the top. There are three peaks in total, two are easy to reach but the third requires a little scrambling, well worth it if you can manage it. Good footwear is essential, especially for the third peak. Mostly people wore trainers but some had walking boots on. Near the bottom there is a small hut on the left run by a guy called Radu serving coconut drinks or mixtures of coconut and fresh fruits. We stopped for 30 minutes to enjoy a fresh coconut and pineapple drink for 200 rupees before heading back into Ella town. Just make sure you ask for the price first!

review_text: Very pleasant walk once out of Ella village. The trail meanders through the tea plantations which are filled with clouds of butterflies. Go early to avoid the heat. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: That's so far the big disappointment of our trip in Sri Lanka. First, it's not a hike, it's a walk. The fact that it takes only 20 minutes to reach the summit makes it extremly cowdy as everyone, of course, is following each other on the tiny path. So the walk is actually stressful as you are constantly pressed by people behind you (even if we were fast walkers). (We had skipped Sirigiya rock for that same reason, the awful crowd.) The rubbish is everywhere along the way, disgusting. I had not read anything about it. Probably people only look up and not where they walk? At the summit, it is so crowdy that you always have some people on your photo. When you wait for your turn to have the view, someone jumps in front of you... it spoils totally the experience. I was really upset at people. Clearly, this is not for me, I prefer the real hike in the mountain, that 99% of these tourists would not be able to do. What about the view? I don't know, I only remember the tourists evertwhere and was not able to take any pictures... Time of the climb: We left town at 8.30 and were at the top at 8.55, so 25 minutes walk. You should not have time to sweat or be thirsty. Sad.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We decided to do a sunset hike given that we did several sunrise hikes. We took a tuk tuk to the base entrance (not near 98 acres resort) for about 200 rupees from town. The hike is fairly easy passing by tea plantations with friendly ladies smiling at you. We said hi and striked up a conversation. They were friendly. We continued upward and lots of stairs initially. Once u get to the top, the last 10 mins requires a bit bouldering and climbing but completely do-able. Kids were doing it while some adults stood back. Highly recommend to do it. Weather was chilly and nice. Couldn’t see the sunset as the mist had set in but we enjoyed it as it was so cooling in the evening. On the way back, we stopped by at 98 acres resort for a celebratory drink. It was pitch dark coming back so bring a torch for the hike. We used a torch and an iPhone flashlight. In case, you are too tired, there are tuk tuk’s at the 98 acres resort waiting for passengers. We didn’t take it. Do the hike for a great view of Ella and all its magnificent views. I’ll let the pictures describe it better.

review_text: A must do if you’re in Ella. You don’t need a tour guide. It’s an easy walk from Ella to the main entrance. With a sign posted walk to the peak. review_text: This is a must do if you are in the area. The walk is either up the steps, or around the ramp on the side - this is misleading as the end part is scrabbling up the side of the hill! Take water with you as it was hot when I went and I was grateful for the water - no watering holes on the way. review_text: A treck to work up a sweat, but nothing too strenuous. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We stayed for only one full day in Ella and made this hike up to Little Adam´s peak during that day. Nice walk through the village or on small paths beside it depending on your choice of route. I strongly recommend the map app "citymaps2go" from Ulmon in your smartphone to find the way yourself. The walk up to the hills are easy and takes your through the tea plantations and you can see workers picking the leaves by hand. The last part of the trekk is steep and takes a bit of fitness to manage. Approx 200 steps on a  steep stair takes you to the first peak. If you want to continue to the other one (with the best view....) it´s a completely different ball game. Real steep path with no steps and full of racks and loose gravel. Be cautious! The views are stunning and after the hike you can refresh at the 98 acres spa and hotel close by or continue to the Nine Arch bridge at Demodara, approx 1,5 mile away.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The way to Little Adam’s Peak begins with a gentle ascent, but at the end it gets steeper and you have also to climb some steps. There’s a small Buddha statue up here which is a nice opportunity for a selfie. You can get here from Ella town within half an hour (walking time) and (depending on your physical condition) within another 30 minutes up to the top. From Little Adam’s Peak you can extend the walk to the Newburgh Tea Factory and the Nine Arches Bridge.

review_text: Approximately 45 minutes in each direction from our rooms (Mount Breeze) on edge of Ella. First 10 minutes on road then bear right on to track through tea plantations. Take path across road that starts to go downhill and follow path around edge of hill avoiding fallen trees! After 15 minutes bridge is suddenly visible below you....fabulous picture stop. After visiting bridge and enjoying a fresh king coconut, walk back into Ella along railway track to complete circular tour of about 2.5 hours. We are in late 60s and found it pretty straightforward!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk starts from the middle of Ella town. Take the B113 Passara Road; there's a sign post at the junction. Keep going to Ella Flower Garden Resort on the right, then take a right onto the narrower tea factory track. Press on - a good track and take a right round the barrier. If you get to the flash resort you've gone too far and missed the right turn. It's possible to turn tuk to this point, but that would be cheating and fairly pointless as it's so close to town. The concrete steps start, then it's a short jaunt to the top. Congratulate yourself and savour the view of Ella Rock. It's worth then continuing along the ridge, dropping down then up again on a slippy mud track, to the next viewpoint to get a better view of Ella Gap. The track continues further down the ridge if you want some more exercise, but you'll have to return the same way. Backtrack, and there is a narrow track at the col that leads you back to the bottom of the steps, or go back up and down the concrete steps. Nice place to stop is the Ella Flower Garden terrace - cold beer and banana roti with a brilliant view.

review_text: The thing to do from Ella is to hike the hour or so to the summit of Little Adams Peak. It is relatively well signposted. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The hike was a relatively easy one with no complicated pathways or rocks to climb on. First half has rocky pathways and second half ends with steep stairs, which can be managed easily. What makes it all completely worth is the view of the sunrise from the peak and the hillside makes a good photo op for "sitting over the edge of the rock" kind of photos.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This was a nice trip to add to our experience of the glorious valleys of Ella. We walked through town and up the road in this direction for about 30 mins or so, then the actual hike begins, about 30 more mins or so to the main peak, which involves a lot of steps and some rocky/earthy scrambling. Once at the top there's a simple Buddha shrine and an optional second hike down the hill and back up a second one. This second hike is a little rougher than the first, but we got through it okay by going slowly and carefully. Craziest part was the pea soup fog that descended while we were on the second peak, which was so thick we couldn't see the first peak any more, or anything below us! When we got  back to the main peak we couldn't see the second one either, and no one was heading to the second one. The point of all that fog talk: probably better to get things in Ella done before 4pm. So far every day the fog descends like crazy at that point and you get a beautifully spooky but not very scenic view of the valley from there on

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It is one of the main attractions in Ella which provides gentle hike with jaw dropping views of plantations and spectacular mountain ranges. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We were looking to do a relatively easy climb in Ella.  It’s simple enough to get to the base of Little Adam’s Peak and the route is pretty clearly marked, so there is no need for a guide.  We started our climb around noon and although it was hot, it was still totally doable for two fairly active people– it took us about 35-40 minutes to reach the top and was well worth the effort.  The views are stunning!  Make sure to continue on to the second peak for a better vantage point; also make sure to bring some water, although there are people selling same at numerous spots along the route.   On the way back, you can opt to walk down or take a tuk-tuk; we chose to stop at the 98 Acres Resort for a well-earned Lion Lager and lunch.

review_text: Ella, 7am start up to the top of Little Adam's Peak. Lovely easy walk from centre of town, accessible and flat until you get to the base of the rock. review_text: We spontaneously decided to hike to Little Adam‘s Peak in the afternoon after having some tea and cake in the area (we had originally planned to go the next morning). Also on the way down don't forget to have a lime coconut drink which is the best feeling after the tiring ride!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is an easy hike and (maximum) 40 mins to climb to the top. We went for the sunset and the path was quite easy except the for the last 15 mins where you have to walk up through steep stairs. Certainly, you will get help from the fellow hikers ! Better to carry some water bottles with you as you won't find any shops at the top. The view from the top was breathtaking and you will find a Buddha statue at the top. However, there's another view point that you should not miss which is another 20 mins walk passing the Buddha statue. Having said that you should only try this if you're not scared of heights as the mountain slope becomes too steep and no safety measures available. But once you get to the top, you will not regret !

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This walk is ideal for anyone.  Not too challenging, the majority of the walk is on a road winding up through the tea plantations. You have beautiful views all around you for the whole walk, not just when you are at the top! The only downside is that due to its accessibility and the views, it means the paths are very busy.  Especially when you get to the top and it becomes narrower and steps, you have to walk slowly because there are so many people. At the top there are two peaks.  Most people stay at the first, but if you want to make it bit more challenging and fun I recommend scrambling down the first peak and up the second.  It is quite steep so be careful of knees. The second peak is a lot less busy to better for photo opportunities. It is easy to reach the start of the walk.  If you walk for about 15 minutes along the road from the centre of Ella, you will reach it.

review_text: Mini Adams peak is the closest and easiest hike in Ella. Got to the entrance in about 15 min walk from Ella town. You can take the bus towards Passara or a tuk tuk. Place got some other names too. So don’t get mis-leaded. Some calls it Punchi Siri Pada, Small Adams Peak, and Little Adams Peak. Hike itself is a worthy experience as you walk through lush green tea estates, talking to locals who are plucking and collecting tea leaves, working in the estate. Go early mornings or late evenings for the best views and it will be less tiring.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Although the climb was a bit challenging for me ( knee problem), it was worth every bit of effort. We were there in August so my advice is to go early in the morning, even if it means returning to the hotel for breakfast afterwards. Keep an eye out for special birds and iguanas along the way. Reaching the top was great, apart from the view it is a calm place and the music from the nearby tea factory just enhanced it. Take your time, the descent is very easy.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It is an approximately 30 mins walk to the top. The views are so amazing, many times better than world's end (horton plains) and ella rock. The steep ella rock is also visible from the top as well. We started for Little Adam's peak early morning at ~7ish and glad we did so, because later it started getting very hot. Starting a little bit earlier at 6 or even 5am, if you want to catch the sunrise, can be a better idea.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Being the relatively unfit couch potato, I underestimated how tiring the climb to the peak would be! It starts off easy enough as a walk through the tea estates, and then the stairs begin. There are approximately 300 steps (I counted!), with some roughly constructed steep rocky pathways I dispersed. However it's very doable, and you can take breathers as often as you like depending on your fitness level. I do recommend taking water along with you for hydration though. We reached the summit at about 8am and stayed until 9, and there were clear views all around at the time. After 9am a thick mist started setting in entirely covering the view below. So I'd suggest asking around about the weather and mist conditions before planning your climb. On your way down stop by at this little hut called Coconut Passion (it's on Google maps!) which is run by a nice lady who serves fresh fruit drinks made with kind coconut water and zero sugar. The pineapple drink was amazing! So refreshing after the heated trek!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We arrived in Ella around 9.30 to start the hike which took approximately 45' if you start from the Main road. You can also take a tuktuk to drop you off from the center. I would advise people to start the hike earlier, because it was already quite crowded especially on the hill top. Beautiful views, fresh air and a relaxed atmosphere will be your reward. It is definitely a must do cause there is not a lot to do in Ella except for the Nine Arch Bridge and Ella Rock (Little Adam's Peak's heavier sister). If you have reached the top take some time to enjoy the view and grab some water (don't go without especially when it is hot like we encountered). After going downhill via the stairs grab something to eat in the 98 acres hotel restaurant: it has a nice atmosphere, good cuisine and fabulous view on Ella Rock. If you have charged batteries after a light lunch or so try to continue your hike to Nine Arch Bridge which is about 20-30' away from the hotel. In stead of going back to the center (left hand side) turn to the right (ask reception of the hotel if you are not sure) at the hotel reception and cashier. Bear in mind that by going this way to the Nine Arch bridge, you will face a narrow rocky pad down to the bridge. We did not do that. We just took a nice spot to have a glance from a higher distance. Also very worth it! Not for people who have a below average condition. After this combo you might be up for a cold drink in one of the village bars. Glad we did this!

A definite must when visiting Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: During my stay in Ella, I climbed the Ella Rock in the morning half and then I took the challenge of climbing the second mountain in the evening. If you are wondering, if doing both Ella Rock and Little Adam's Peak in one-day is feasible or not, my answer is it's "doable". Of course you need decent physical fitness, and mental readiness to do this, but it's possible. From Ella town to entrance point to Little Adams Peak is about 1 KM. A Threewheeler guy will charge you LKR 200 for this, but I decided to walk that distance as well! (It will take less than 30 minutes). Then the climb up was about 1.5KM, which will take about a maximum 1.5 hours. Unlike Ella Rock, the path is a well built road up to about 80% of the total distance. Rest, is a set of stone stairs which you can easily climb. View along the way is very beautiful, as you are supposed to walk through a Tea Estate. I spent about 1 hour on the top, enjoying the magnificent view there. Climb down is much easier, it took me only another hour or so to be back at Ella town.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We first walked along the rail tracks to the 9 arches bridge, then made our way over to climb Little Adam's peak. This makes a nice loop. On the Ella side of the bridge, there is a cafe and area where the tuktuks park. Across the track from that is a stand selling coconut water with a set of concrete steps leading up the hill behind it. Those take you to a dirt path along the ravine that offers an excellent view of the bridge in the afternoon when the sun is coming from the west. If you continue walking along this trail (stepping over a number of felled trees that have been lain out to hinder walking along the path), you will come out into a little farming area near a stream and continuing along the largest path, you'll come to the road between Ella and little Adam's peak. Turn left and walk a little ways to reach the start of the accent. If you climb the peak first, bear left/head straight onto the road to Ella and then turn right off onto the path alongside the cream and red/orange house a little a ways out of the very settled area of town. I'll try to post a photo of this turn-off here later.  It will lead you in the reverse direction described above. Very nice views up top here, good path and easy to find. Nice hike for younger kids too if they have some stamina.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It is a easy trail as the slopes are gentle. Most of the trail have wide path or staircase. You get to see Ella Gap as well as Ella rock from the top. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A hike to Little Adam's Peak needs no money, cost you little time and will reward you with excellent views! It is a must-do experience for travelers to Ella, adults, elderly in a good condition and children alike, because this is what Ella is so famous for: the views! Best time to visit is during the early morning hours to have the clearest views and the heat will not beat you as hard as during midday and afternoon. Easy to find.. Go to 98 Acres Hotel on foot, by bus (Passara direction), by tuktuk or by scooter, whatever you prefer. There is a direction sign to Little Adam's Peak near the hotel. The footpath after the entrance gate is very easy to walk and offers you wonderful views on the tea gardens on the slopes of the hills. At the end, right in front of you you'll find a staircase with roughly 300 steps which brings you to the top. The views on a clear day are stunning. On the right sight you can see the famous Ella Rock, it can't be missed. On the summit of Little Adam's Peak there are two small Buddha Statues and when you look left at it you'll notice that this mountain has an extension of several more small peaks. If you want to go there, you must consider that part is a far more strenuous hike and not suitable for for children. Take the same way back to the entrance gate. If you take your time staying at the top and taking pictures on the way it will take you about 2 hours. Take a water bottle and some snacks. Coming back to the entrance gate and turn right, follow the entire path to the end end you will reach the main road. If you plan to visit the Nine Arches Bridge, cross the road and you'll find a trek you can follow. It will lead you to the direction of this bridge. Keep following the un-carpeted road until you see some sign boards.

review_text: Great views all the way! There are these local women who smile at you to take photos with them but expect to pay them something for it! location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy hike for all levels and one of the landmarks of Ella. More experienced/fit hikers can easily do it in the same day as a more difficult one (we did Ella Rock in the morning and Little Adam's just after that). Trail can be started and ended either right by Ella Flower Garden Resort or inside 98 Acres Resort & Spa, further down the road. Starting in one and ending in the other would make for a 2.5 km hike, mostly over gravel/sand road. Overall, it took us just over 1 hour, including stops for photos, but we hike on a somewhat fast pace, so I would say it's a 1-2 hours activity for most people. The downside: the stairs when you actually reach the peak. It's not that they are very difficult to climb or anything like that, it's just that they really kill the mood of any hike.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Cons: Can be full of other backpackers and the like and best done at dawn so go early early. Pros: The view is amazing and with a bit of extra effort you'll get away from the crowd. Wake up early and do this with the fresh morning sun or even better sunrise. The route from Ella town is relatively simple and even if you go slightly off track it's not hard to get to the top. At the top take in the view of Ella Rock and the sunrise. Be warned the usual grab bag of hemp wearing hippies, selfie takers, backpackers drinking from the night before, and a lot of stray dogs can ruin the vibe but don't worry. There are four further peaks across from the main peak each slightly lower than the last but each offering a fabulous if not better view.  The first is only metres away, but three to five are a bit harder to get to and the paths not as well used. Number three being the hardest to get to and the reason most people are put off. Don't be, getting to the fifth and lowest peak provides an amazing unobscured view that is breathtaking.

review_text: A must do hike for all fit families. We walked from Ella Flower Garden Hotel side trek. First part consists of slowly ascending trek which can accommodate small cars and tuk tuk. Next part consists of ascending trek with mostly large Rocks and gravel. Final part consists of either a steep set of cement stairs which takes you up on a shorter route or a winding gravel road which is longer but manageable if you have issues with high steps. Then you approach the first of three peaks. Then move left towards the next peak. And the real mini adams peak lies in the third one, which requires a bit of guts to conqure the narrow trek. It's a bit of a tough climb. Almost all foreigners were grasping for breath for few minutes. But the third peak top, if you can make is breathtaking. Even the other two peaks offer some amazing views. This is a very safe trek. You occasionally meet many foreign tourists climbing. Clear treks, and clean route. Lots of traffic bushes and licht greenery around. Kids too can come with few rests in between the climb. One of the nicest hikes I've done. It took 19min to come down from peak to bottom. Some 2250 steps. The highest point is 1045m above sea level, whereas you start it from 926m at the road level. A must do!

review_text: As a Colorado native, I found both Ella Rock and Little Adam's Peak to be fairly tame. review_text: This is a short hike with a good reward. The hike is free and it takes around 30 - 60 minutes from the town to the peak depending on your pace. review_text: This is an easy walk to the summit and well worth taking a packed breakfast to enjoy an early morning sunrise at the summit. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: From Ella town (near the railway station), take the Namunukula Road for about 2-3 kilometers. The turn-off is to the right, and is marked by signs. You then walk through a forest reserve, where several endemic birds - including the Ceylon Grey Hornbill - can sometimes be seen. Avoid using vehicles. It is the walk, and the accompanying quietness, that is an important prelude to the beautiful vistas that greet you after a relatively short climb. Make sure that your shoe have a good grip, as a fall may easily become dangerous. The winds at the top can be quite strong, so be sure to hold firmly onto lens caps, scarves, hats, et cetera. The sunset is obscured by the Ella Rock that looms to the West. Part of the walk is through a tea estate. After descending from the rock, you can take a 1-2 hour detour that will take you to the Nine-Arches railway bridge. Be careful of opportunistic cafes that charge usurious amounts for small meals.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adams Peak hike starts from the track next off to the right on the corner ofElla's Flower Garden Hotel/ Cafe. Cafe has great Sri Lankan coffees, western breakfasts and cool fruit drinks perfect for some energy before or after the hike. View here in equally amazing. Tuk tuk from the town, if scooter can park near there. 40-50 minutes hike to the peak walking through tea plantations is a nice stroll. Good views of the valleys and Ella Rock. Definitely the warm up to Ella Rock hike we did in the afternoon. LAP in my opinion gives you a better view. ER a more demanding hike and sense of achievement and effort - abit of a shocker in terms of directions/ locals, we were close to turning round until we got some proper directions from other travelers descending. We did the Nine Arches Train Bridge in between, nice old bridge to check out. If your lucky you'll see a train come through while your there. Trains are super slow so all locals/ travelers use the tracks as a footpath. Did these 3 in about 6-7 hours. We were on a scooter which was a help to get to the starting points and cut the time in between. Bought some delicious Sri Lankan street snacks on Main Street to chomp on throughout. Def sports/ hiking shoes activity. Overall a fun day in Ella, good for some exercise before/ after days lazing on the southern beaches.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This hike can be completed in less than an hour (not necessarily including walk from Ella) and is fairly easy. We started around 8am and it wasn't too busy but was filling up by the time we were coming down.  Stunning view from the top, excellent photo-ops - would definitely recommend! While a map is not required for the route, you may need some direction to get from your hotel - there is absolutely no signage on the road so it can be hard to know if you're on track.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy walk, great views. Well worth a couple of hours to visit. We went at sunset and it made it all the more beautiful. The summit gets a little crowded with lots of great self opportunities but plenty of space for everyone to share the beauty. Give it a go!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is an easy walk outside the Ella town itself. I am not going to lie, there are a few stairs and I was happy to reached the top a little puffed. For those of us a little less active you might need to stop and catch your breath once or twice but please don't let that stop you as I saw people around my parent's age make it to the summit so take your time, it wont take more than 30 minutes from the first step till the top. The view is definitely worth it and no doubt you will get some great photographs for sure. Most of the climb is under trees and with a slight breeze it is a very comfortable climb up temperature-wise. For anyone traveling with children please be aware there are no handrails on the stairs or at the summit so take extra care its a long way down.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We headed up Little Adam's Peak at 6:00 a.m. To beat the heat and the crowds. Others had the same idea, but it was overall a good plan and the top was not too crowded. A Surprisingly quick hike--40 minutes up from our guesthouse, close to the center of Ella. A little faster coming down. We are Two folks in their mid sixties, still pretty active, and we found this to be a very pleasant walk. Views were fantastic.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We took a tuk tuk to the beginning of the walk which made it quite easy, nothing too physical.  Great views on the way there and back, and from the top, and on the walk up.  Very pretty area of Sri Lanka, would be easy for children as well.  We started early, and by the time we were coming down those folks who had started in Ella itself - not an unmanageable distance by any means - were arriving just a little hot.  So if you aren't in it for the mileage, start early, get taken by tuk tuk to the beginning of the walk, and beat the crowds and the heat.

review_text: This was an easy stroll from the town of Ella. Manageable in flip flops, but trainers would probably be recommended! We arrived at the start of the trail at 9am and there were quite a few tourists but not an annoying amount. The trail starts by walking though beautiful tea plantations. There are a few road side cafe huts to by coconuts and drinks from served by really friendly locals. We climbed to the top of little Adams peak and found a tree to relax under, enjoying the stunning views from the shade. Plenty of space at the top for everyone, there was a bit of tourist traffic on the steps up, but it's well worth a visit! We are going back to Ella next year and will revisit this peak.

review_text: The hike is pretty short and easy. Starting from Ella town it takes maybe 40 minutes up. The view from the peak is amazing, looking at the surrounding mountains, including Ella Rock. Would definitely recommend doing this hike!

review_text: Best place to start mornings in Ella. Quite an easy walk to the top before the step. Steps can be a bit slippery after rains. Great views during the trek and from the top. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This site is accessible by walking (not hiking) along a wide paved/rock path to a hill overlooking the Ella Valley.  Once on top, there are opportunities to walk a bit farther to other viewpoints to watch the sun rise or set, depending on the time of day.  We were able to walk the distance from the trailhead to the top in 25 minutes, and we were not in a big hurry. The views are nice as was the sunset when we were there, and the ambiance of the setting and our location was quite nice.  This would probably change with several other visitors on top at the same time.  We were 4 of about 25 other people the evening we were there. Appropriate footwear would be light hikers, tennis shoes, or good sandals (Chacos).  Hiking poles are unnecessary.

review_text: A good walk in the morning up Little Adam's Peak is amazing. You will see tea plantations along the way. The last part to the top is a long flight of steps but is easy. Try to go early in the morning to avoid the hot sun. A pair of proper walking shoes is recommended.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The Little Adam's peak is a 30 minute hike (moderate fitness level) from the Reception of 98 acres. The first 200 meters is on gravel and then steps to the top. It is not difficult at all and can be easily climbed. A lot of people mistake it for Ella Rock. The view from the top is breathtaking. You can even see the Ravana Falls from here. Best time to go is early morning and be back by 10:30am as the climb / descent may get hot after that. Keep about half an hour for soaking in the views. Would not suggest climb or descent before sunrise or after sunset as it may get difficlut to navigate some steps without appropriate light. Must do if in Ella! If you have more time and good fitness level then try the main Adam's peak or Ella rock. From whatever I heard from the people around we picked the Little Adam's peak over the Ravana cave.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Walk up is easy, except the last part where one has to climb up a number of steps to reach the peak. However, I believe there is another path without steps which one can take if not comfortable climbing steps. There is really nothing much to do in Ella, nonetheless the stunning views from little adam's peak makes the town a worthwhile stop when in Sri Lanka. Took about 1 hour to reach the top from main Ella town centre, at a leisurely pace and with lots of photo-taking stops in between. Spent about 45 mins at the top, soaking in the incredible view. Walk back down to Ella town centre should take around another 30 mins.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Great views at the top, but there are LOTS of steps. The walk is easier than Ella Rock and you don't need a guide, but that doesn't make it an 'easy' climb. Although with a reasonable level of fitness you will make it and the view is well worth it!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: If you're looking for a long intense hike, this one isn't for you. It's a very short little loop up to Little Adam's peak. Great views from the top and very pleasant. If you have a chance to pick-nick up there on a nice day, would be totally worth it. Careful the sun is strong in Ella!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a must if visiting Ella! It takes about half an hour to walk from the city to the top and there isn't too much climbing. You get to walk past all the tea pickers on the way. The highlight for us, along with the magnificent views, was on the way down when we went into Coco Passion. I'm not exaggerating when I say that I had the BEST fruit juice I have ever tasted - we tried the coconut & passion fruit and coconut & lemon blends. Family run business on the side of the dirt track, as you come back down it's on your left maybe 10 mins from the top. Pop in here for the best juice you'll have in Sri Lanka! Run by a lovely man who was happy to answer lots of questions we had about the tea plantations and his wife who made the juices. You have to pop in here. If I was staying here longer I'd be back there every day.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: After spending the night in Ella with srilankanishatours my driver Nisha suggested we do the walk upto little Adams peak which was perfect, the scenery is beautiful and although a couple of steep climbs and scrambles, not too strenuous definitely worth the effort for a photo opportunity.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Suprisingly easy to get to the top of little Adams Peak. On the top, after 1202 steps you can enjoy a magnificant view. Free entrance, at least when we visited. Enjoy 😀

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is easy and you can walk to it from the centre of Ella.  The path itself is mostly paved and easy to walk on. Remember to turn right about half way. If you are in a hurry the start of the path to the summit and back can be done in about 40 minutes.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It took us two hours to do this walk. You go through tea fields slowly climbing up. Then there is a stair case taking you up and then a steep path and you reach the first top. Enjoy the view there. Then go further, climbing down a bit and then another steep path up. Second top, again very nice views. Again it goes down and up to the third peak. Really nice view from there! You could go further but we stopped here. We went back down this third peak and at the bottom (before going up the second peak) there is a path going right. That goes back without climbing again the first and second peak. Most people seem not to know. You walk through high grass and some forest and then meet the path you came just before the steep climb to the first peak.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We wanted to do Adam's Peak, but didn't end up having enough time, so we found this as an alternative. It's certainly not the same experience, but it was still marvelous. The hike (walk) is mostly on a gravel path and isn't too steep until the top ascent. At that point it switches to stairs and requires more effort and focus.  The view at the top is stunning- you can see Ella rock, the falls, and a great overall view of the amazing hills of Ella.   We zipped right down and then stopped at 98 acres for a bite to eat (mixed reviews on this one if focused on food and service and great reviews for the view).

A little kindness is all it takes and you'll leave with the feeling of witnessing a gorgeous landscape and the positivity of helping another.

review_text: The summit of Little Adam's Peak is very easy to reach and the view down the Ella gap is fantastic. Note that it can be very windy there so take some warm cloths with you, some people went there to see the sunset and had to leave early because they were cold.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The steps at the end will get you out of breath, but this is an easy hike for almost everyone to enjoy with a stunning view as reward when you get to the peaks. Only the very last part towards another hill at the top was too scary for me (afraid of heights, or better: of falling). Don't go to far by tuck tuck, the walk up through the tea plantation is actually really nice, too. You'll pass the helipad of a luxury hotel on one side and poor living quarters on the other. Don't worry about the occasional attempt to sell something to or beg something off you along the way. Everyone we encountered accepted a No as answer as well.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point

review_text: Little Adam's Peak is supposedly a site of worship, we could see that at the top. We walked from the center of town, through tea estates to the top, meeting few locals while we trekked. review_text: A wonderful short walk/scramble to be rewarded with a terrific view. Very peaceful as Shepherds walked their cows along the dirt tracks and the tea plantation rustled with the breeze. Highly recommend and probably best thing to do in Ella. Hot tip: after the hike go for a tea/beer at 98 Acres nearby.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point

Definitely a must do activity.

review_text: Going up Little Adam's Peak is a very pleasant walk through green tea fields and lush hills. The first part is an easy walk on a good path, after which you need to climb about 200 steps or so. Then a short dodgy path and then you're on the first of three hilltops. The second is an easy walk but the third one requires going down a steep hill on what can hardly be called a path. Quite doable, but not for those with vertigo. Either way, views over the surrounding countryside are great from each peak and well worth the short climb.

review_text: Often referred to as the easier climb, relative to Ella's rock, little Adam's peak was still jaw dropping. Most of the climb was easy and totally safe. On our way down we stopped at 98 acre restaurant and treated ourselves to a great lunch with a great view. A win win combination.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: One of the best things to do in Ella. Must visit if you come to Ella. As I always prefer, I rented a bike for the day, and drove down to all my key locations including the base of little Adams peak. From there, we climbed up the top. After a while, there are two ways to go further up, take the stairs or walk the small climbing road. Stairs are around 300 in number and faster, but make your climb much more difficult. The road is not marked very clearly close to the top, and you need to figure your way up without much help. There are 3 peaks you can go to once you reach the top, all 3 have some breathtaking views. As soon as we started our decent it stated raining pretty heavily making the way down slightly slippery and difficult. Otherwise, it's an easy walk and must try.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A must do for any visitor to Ella. The peak itself isn't all that difficult to find: once you find the ella flower garden resort on Passara road, head along the signposted path. After walking past a small village and tiny hidden Hindu temple beside a playing field, you'll come to a little intersection with a sign pointing to Cafe 98 Acres, or some other Cafe. Turn right and head along the road marked by the car gate. You'll soon be rewarded with amazing views of the surrounding area. In all directions, a sea of green. The peak itself is quite difficult to scale with lots of bare paths and steep sections, but the walk up there is trivial. Lots of people around if you need help. Bring water. Enjoy.

review_text: There are a number of pleasant walks around Ella, and the walk to and up Little Adam's Peak is one of the 'must do' attractions in the area.  Great views of the Ella Gap and the surrounding area.  A good level of fitness required for the climb up the steep steps of the trail up the hill.  Nice to stop by the restaurant of the nearby 98 Acres resort on the way back.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A relatively easy trail walk that serves as a good introduction to the scenic landscape surrounding Ella. Can be tackled by young children also but perhaps allow two hours for total joinery from centre of town. Final 15 minutes requires navigating 160  concrete steps. Good foot ware and water a must.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The climb for this is not too strenuous and relatively quick and the view you get at the top is definitely a winner! My partner and I felt this was a great experience to fit in as because it does not take a full day like Adam's peak it is a lot more relaxing and you can also walk to the nine arch bridge which is not far if that is on your list.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Ella's little Adams peake is a nice accessable peak not far from Ella center. The trail starts about 1 km from the center and the hike up is moderately easy. Will take your breath if you are an office worker, and nice easy excersize if you are in good shape.  Put on good walking shoes and bring water and snacks. There are two peaks. The later one is much more demanding and you will need some agility to get there. The scenery up is great to sit and admire ones you are up. There are a few cafes on the way and you can by a picknic basket from the Garden restaurant in the start of the trail. You will have company on your picknic from the stray dogs at the peak.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Took a very leisurely stroll due to the time of day we started (10.30am). Walked through the tea plantation and final stage some quick steep steps but plenty of room to allow those coming down and those coming up to pass.  It didn't feel crowded at all and once you reach the top there are quite a few summits to choose which one to take your "king of the world" photo from!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Either 20minute walk or short Tok Tok trip to start from town centre. No sign at walk start, so ask locals or travellers. Your Tok Tok driver will know. Gentle gradient past tea plantations and villages along side road. Consistently rewarding you with views down the valley beyond Ella pass. Then a very short steep stepped climb along a footpath to the top. Look down onto the low country and across to Ella Rock. Allow a hour or so for the return walk to trailhead.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A great little walk to the top of a hill about 1-2km out of Ella, offering quite spectacular views of the surrounding mountains and countryside from the top. It's only about 1km in total (from the start of the path but not always signposted. Thankfully, there were enough other people doing it to simply follow them - so no guide necessary! There's around 320 steps to navigate along the way but a lovely way to start, or end, a day in Ella. Wouldn't recommend doing in the heat of the day.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Great quick and easy climb. Nothing like the real Adams Peak! Incredible views. Stop along the way at a little coconut hut "coconut passion" for a coco-pineapple drink, blended for you and served in a coconut with a straw. So delish and refreshing.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: it was really nice view from the top, the hike was quite easy, it took us 20 min from the main road, we came around 7:30 am and the view was very nice, no fog or mist, we really loved it, it is suitable for families with children too,

review_text: A very pleasant stroll from Ella. The gentle walk up through the tea plantation was easy. It was not pleasant to meet a young girl and her Grandmother begging. review_text: I loved this walk/hike. We started from town, and missed the turn up the peak, but we managed to get back on the road, by taking up the ramp for the 98 Acres Hotel Resort. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A leisurely 45 minute walk up to Little Adam's Peak is definitely worth it. Only gets steep and somewhat challenging for the last section up the stairs, should be achievable for most people. The views are amazing, you can see across Ella Gap to Ella Rock. Definitely one of the highlights of our time in Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It takes about 1 hour from central Ella to go to Little Adam's peak where you get great views of the Ella Gap and Ella Rock. The walk towards the rock is straighforward and quite easy and already provides great views. to get to the top itself is a little steeper with stairs at the first part but anybody in a normal condition should be able to do it and the views from the top are extremely rewarding 360 degrees around.  Go in the morning, clouds gather most afternoons, mornings have most chance of sunshine and clear views.
