location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy to reach from Ella by foot walking along road from Information Booth in town.  Once there the scenery is breathtaking.  We continued to walk along ridge to the farthest Peak.  That was a lot more tricky as there is a steep rocky descent and ascent requiring a lot of scrambling... not for the faint hearted and not recommended in the wet either. We stopped for a lovely lunch at 98 Acres on the return trip.  Very nice spot in tea plantation overlooking the mountains.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It is definitely worth the sweat to get up the mountain as the bee that opens I front of you is simply breathtaking! Be prepared for.a steep climb and don't go up there in Flipflops. It is also quite windy on the top. Take tuktuk to get to the gates of adam's peak road - after the gates you still have plenty of opportunities to power out but the tuktuk driver can shorten your suffering a bit. On the road there are kids that would like you to take a picture of them - don't be a cheapskate and fork out 100 rupee for them - their parents collect tea on the hills and work hard for their bread.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: But great fun none-the-less. This is a sharp little climb to get some fantastic views of the valleys around Ella. There is a mixture of stairs and basic track to get to the first of three little peaks. Whilst the first is marginally the highest, the third is the more difficult climb. If you reasonably confident on your feet, all three are worth doing. If you are a little wobbly on your feet definitely skip the third! You will be spoilt with sensational 360 degree views. Highly recommended.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The climb up is not hard at the beginning however there are a lot of steps at the end which could be easily done if you take your time. It's worth it! The view at the top is fabulous and it's an easy walk down! The street dogs are used to taking tourists up there!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Wasn't expecting much for this hike as we've done a couple of hikes in other countries with spectacular views and Mother Nature wasn't feeling particularly on point when we started our hike. We started the descent from our BnB in the mountains and worked our way up to Litttle Adam's Peak. There weren't many signs around but the locals were great at giving guidance. Along the way we were treated to lush greenery and the landscape of the mountains! There is even a small green tea plantation where you will circle, before heading upwards to the peak. Be forewarned, taking a picture of the tea plantation workers will cost you a small fee. You can even stop by 98 acres cafe for coffee and a spot to appreciate the views.. Overall - great hike for families and older folks. Was pleasantly surprised with the picturesque views we had!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: If you're in Ella this is a must do for two reasons; 1. It's a very easy trek with no complications in finding your way. 2. Awesome view from the top with very little effort. The climb (well mostly a walk and then towards the end some concrete steps to climb) will take you about 45 mins up and maybe 20 mins back down. You don't need hardcore hiking shoes but you'd be more comfortable in good shoes obviously. But you can easily do this in sandals too. If you're climbing during colder months like Dec make sure to summit before 9am as you run the risk of having the mist set in covering your view from top. Watching the sunrise from the top is recommended for sure!! Also bring a good camera cuz you're going to get some very good shots ;) even a few daring ones. But always be safe first!

review_text: You need to hike up little bit ,but don't be worry there is a path and stairs, you can see easily.Little raincoat is enough,if you're planning to stay after 6-7 pm ,take a torch with you.Because in the dark ,it is not easy to hike down ,belive me.We did it. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is easily reached without a guide, you can walk from Ella town and lots of locals will help you if you can't find the way. There is a clearly signposted track off by Chill Out cafe, it's a pleasant walk and only on the last bit is there some stairs and a steep path. Once on the top there is stunning views of Ella Rock, Ella Gap and all the surrounding tea plantations. I would recommend taking the left path once on the top to the left side peak, but it's a bit of a climb up and down! Possibly the most rewarding hour or two of your life. Get up early before the heat and go enjoy.

review_text: We have expected it to be quite a challenging walk, but to our surprise we had a perfectly paved path and then it became a bit steep - proper stairs. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: From ella town, have to take passara road. There are two easily traceable starting points as I know. One starting near from elle flower garden resort and tge ither near 98acres small car park. Both spots are just by the elle passara road. From Elle town, there maybe about 2.5-4kms to tge startibg point uphill. We saw tourists walkibg to tgese poibts as well, also you may take a tuktuk ride. We entered from 98acres resort side. You pass the resort entrance and you see their spa and reception. Then walkibg alobg tea fields you come to the steps and then end with naturally created paths uphill. I would not say it was easy for me to climb and was panting after climbibg fir about 10 minutes  if you are not a frequent walker, you will find it a bit tiring, like me. (This was my first climb/trek) But the whole climb was about 45mins (with multiple stops). Take frequent rests on the way to pant and  rest so it will not be that hard. The path to climb is quite spacious I would say so that it gives space for you to stop n rest. Do not forget your water bottles, I would say atleast 3/4 litres for whole trip for 1 person. No refreshments along the way. When you reach the top, you know it was all worth it, its beautiful!!!! Peaceful and so relaxing. We found multiple spots(huge rocks) to sit and relax. Dont forget to take some snacks to sit and enjoy the view on the top. Spend about 30 minutes to 1 hour on the top or even more. You can see the popular 98acres resort from the other side of the mountain when you are climbing. There are three peaks on the top. We only went for two. The third one required further climbing down and up again so we did not try it, maybe next time. You can see wibdibg roads lots of greenery. So peaceful. Can spend ebture day there. Climbing down will take only about 30 minutes or less. We took some pics with tea plucking ladies and they asked for money very humbly but we went off after one pic. People around ella are so helpful and always willing to help. We saw this everywhere we went. Fell in love with the place.

If you're staying in Ella town and don't want to walk all the way, you can always hitch a ride or take a tuk to the car park at the bottom of the hill. From thereon it's about a 30 min walk. You go through a tea plantation and a colony of tea estate workers and come to a security gate which you need to squeeze through. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: TAKE DOG TREATS!!! Absolutely enjoyed both Ella Rock and Little Adams Peak - Ella Rock is more demanding and one can easily get lost. We hired a human guide to help us through the goat tracks up to the top of Ella Rock.  Once we arrived on the top we met 2 friendly dogs who lead the way back down the mountain right back to our hotel door. I mentioned this to the hotel owner who said that some of the stray dogs have become tour guides!!!  The next morning we headed out to conquer  Little Adams Peak -and  to our amazement the same 2 dogs saw us and started walking along with us .  As we headed up the road we joined by 4 more stray dogs one with a terrible broken leg - all of them lead  the way to the top of Little Adams Peak.  It really was an incredible experience and I urge everyone  travelling to Ella to take some healthy dog treats and extra water (as up the top of Little Adams Peak is a mother and her very young puppies).  If your a dog lover - you will appreciate the company.

review_text: We were supposed to climb Adam's Peak, but the weather forecast wasn't very favorable, so we took the route to Ella and hiked its little brother instead. Not a bad idea after all. It was a very easy hike. Coming from the main road at Ella junction, we reached the peak after roughly 50 minutes (small Asians here! :D) and after missing a sign near 98 acres. The first 20 minutes was an uphill cemented road, with lots of hostels, cafes, houses, and vehicles. Then you start the more natural path by the side of the mountain then on to a few tea plantations. Got to photograph a few tea pickers and kids along the way :) The view at the top is spectacular. The path to the other lower peak looked dangerous, but was actually easy. The view is basically the same with the summit though, so probably not so much worth another 10minutes if you're already tired. Try to avoid flipflops as the path gets rocky and dusty. And suggest to avoid loose bags or carry-ons as you'll need to hold on to rocks esp going to the "other peak".

review_text: This is a small hike that may take around 30 minutes. Most people can do it taking a break every once in a while. review_text: This was our 2nd favourite activity in Ella, after Ella Rock. Walk down the main road, then turn left by the junction. Walk past Ella Super, and the vegetarian restaurant. When you get to a flower nursery on your right hand side, turn right. There are signs. Continue up the path/stairs until you reach the peak. The trip takes approx. 1 hr from Ella and back again. It's a nice stroll among the tea plantations. If you fancy more waking after Little Adam, you can easily keep on walking in other directions among the plantations.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: One of the few attractions in Sri Lanka with free entrance. Having been to Adam's Peak and as a seasoned hiker, this is a lovely walk in the park suitable for all ages. Saw plenty families taking it easy on this hike. Summit meanders to 2-3 different peaks where you could take photos with Ella Rock backdrop. Was a bit unclear and fogged up as it's October nevertheless glad I went, it was worth it!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My friends and I hiked (walked) up here before sunrise and it was our best decision of the weekend. If you go at sunrise, I'd recommend finding the entrance to the trail the day before because it's difficult to find if you are not familiar with the area. Also, you don't need a local to guide you, so don't waste your money.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I believe Little Adam's peak is a must in Ella (we skipped Ella rock as our host told us this is much better)! Maybe this is not so easy to come by (do not go in your slippers,it could be the problem to climb up the rocks),but it is really worth it! If you get lost on the way ask the locals,they will be glad to help you. Also,if you are bad in climbing,please ask someone or just do the stairs part and miss the other rock,the view on this part is great too.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We really didn't know where the path was but set out down the railway tracks with a few other tourists.After taking a wrong turning we found ourself at a friendly farmers house. The farmer became our guide for the next four hours.It was totally worth having a guide as there are lots of tracks and it would be easy to take the wrong pathway.It is quite a hard walk but worth the effort for some excercise and the views.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Very easy walk up to the peak, definitely don't take a guide!! We decided against the stairs on the way up and we're winding round the dirt road, with some spectacular views. Got to the top at about 5pm and it gets increasingly busy from then with other like minded people waiting for a sunset. So grab your spot early and chill out with the little dogs at the top. Sunset is well worth the wait and everyone leaves almost the second it's gone down, so wait to avoid the rush on the stairs down. Have to check this out if you're in Ella!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We climbed to the top of little Adams peak at around 4pm and it was a great time to do so. It is not too hard if you pay close attention to the signs but we did take a bit of a detour due to not concentrating! You don't need a guide to get there though! Once you find the garden centre there is signage from then on. The first half is a super easy slight ascent up flat road, the last bit is concrete steps which may be difficult for anyone who can be a little unsteady on their feet. Although we were followed up by 2 kids who looked about 6 and they seemed to have no trouble! We were followed the whole way up by a little dog (our guide) and he seemed to have no trouble with the stairs! Gorgeous panoramic views at the top featuring Ella rock! A must do if you are in Ella!

review_text: We walked to Adams Peak from our hotel in Ella. It took about an hour from Ella to reach the top, climbing about 300 steps. The walk was easy until you get to the stairs, and then it's a bit of a climb. Once you are at the top the view is amazing. Highly recommended.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We did this the day after we climbed Ella Rock so this was a far easier proposition! Its a gradual path virtually all the way up and only gets a bit steep at the end (it probably took about 45 mins in total). We saw lots of colourful lizards on the way and the weather was superb....go in the morning! The views are superb at the top especially of Ella Rock across the 'Gap'. Absolutely a must do walk in Ella and particularly a good choice for those who don't fancy the more rigorous climb to Ella rock.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The climb wasn't hard at all. You don't need experience for this hike. If you are walking here you should have a drink at Coco passion. They mix fresh coconuts with passion-, lemon- or pineapplejuice. This is a really good combination. It will make the  trip even more nice!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: About a 1km walk from the centre of town to the start of the path through the streets of Ella. Walk down the Passara Road until you come to the 1km marker post. The Ella Flower Garden Resort is on the right. The path sets off as a concrete road and then into a firm track.  There are various turns but it is reasonably clear which way to go. There was just one turn that was unclear - by a roti hut take the left track. The final ascent is up numerous concrete steps and when you arrive at the top you are afforded some magnificent views.  Well worth expending the energy! We would recommend to give yourself enough time to return in daylight and there is no need for a guide. It took us approx 45 mins to reach the top.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Climbed this hill early starting from the chillout guesthouse. Started in the dark at 0515 to arrive at the top in time for sunrise. Take a torch as it is still very dark at this time and you may be followed by one or two harmless stray dogs. The walk is a concrete road through tea plantations for the first half followed by steps to the top. The walk up is easy going and takes no more than 25 minutes. There are good views at the top and the sunrise is great with clear skies. The main downside to this walk is that you will see tons of rubbish on the way down lining the path. It wouldn't take long for some local people to clear the place up as this can ruin the experience. Overall worth a visit if you are in the area.

review_text: Best activity to do around Ella. I drove up with a scooter a long way, but you can also walk, it is an easy walk on a wide path. Make sure you have more than an hour before sunsetonce you are on the top so you have tim to explore the 4 mountain tops.

review_text: Reasonably easy hike with great views and well worth it! Took us about 45 mins to get to the top (from Ella town) and that included a lot of stopping for photos! Great walk through the tea plantations. And if you have some energy left take another 45 min walk to the 9 arch bridge. Which requires a little bit more climbing down rugged terrain!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked here today from nine arches bridge. It was a very doable hike up the hill, stairs almost all the way up, can easily be done in half an hour. The views from the top were lovely. On the way there you pass by a tea plantation, and the scenery was beautiful.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Went up for sunrise, nothing incredible to justify a sunrise walk. In fact views are clearer as the say goes on. But completely worth it nonetheless. An early rise for us allowed us to go to the nine arch bridge, and the green tea factory in the area before breakfast at 9:30. And we did Ella Rock in the afternoon at our ease. When leaving the peak at the end of the descent road turn right at the T-junction instead of left back the way you came. This will take a quicker nicer way to the green tea factory (opens at 8:30am) and the nine arch bridge (9:20am for first train passing).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a lovely hike that can be accessed on foot from Ella town centre. The walk winds is way up via a track through some luscious green tea plantations. The final section is a series of steps that lead to the top. The views are beautiful in all directions from the top.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is the perfect little outing in Ella. About an hour to ascend and 30-40 mins to descend it's great to stretch your legs, see the tea plantations, and take in the stunning views of the valley. Definitely recommended if you have time! However, go in the morning. If you leave it till lunch time the clouds usually come in mid to late afternoon (sometimes earlier) and you definitely don't want to be caught in that!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Lovely walk and beautiful views both on the way to the top and the top itself.  I would suggest personally going at 7-8am as not as busy but much more bearable in the heat you also get to see tea workers in the fields.  At the top we had stunning panoramic views of Ella and miles into the distance.  We also had many friendly dogs who would join us on various parts of the journey (we gave them so food and water at the peak which they loved).  The walk takes about 40mins and the first part is very comfortable and steady walk up roads, however, the last part whilst completely do-able is much steeper steps and if old or young worth noting.  We also stopped off at 98 acres hotel on the way back to have drink from there restaurant, it is a very lovely hotel with amazing views and despite being slightly more expensive than a drink in the town the views were worth this.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It is quite easy to find. It is down the road from the Ella Town where the Ella Hotel is. Almost anyone can direct you. There us a small shop with nice flower at the turn off to the hike up to the peak. It is quite easy as the initial bit winds around tea estates and towards the latter part it is a few staircases up to the peak. Would rate it easy to moderate. Walking shoes will help. There are great photo opportunities at the peak. Early morning climb recommended as the view is amazing. If you wish you can view a Tea factory on the way up or down

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: What a wonderful hike. In contrast to Ella Rock, the trail is very well marked and developed. It's almost impossible to get lost. Although it is very popular and you will encounter numerous other hikers, everybody you meet seems to be in a cheerful mood. We met people in ages from 5 to 70. The trail winds its way leisurely through a scenic tea estate, with numerous flowering trees lining the path. It is a very gradual incline for most of the way. Then the path becomes steep, with a winding stairway for the final ascent. The steps are well-maintained, however, and the views at the top are a great reward for your efforts.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We decided to go see little Adam's Peak on our trip to Ella. It is VERY easy to find your way up there by yourself, and you should award yourself the walk. If you get tired very easy then don't take the trip. The first way up the hill is very easy (and we are NOT climbers at all) then you get to the stairs, and it gets a little harder, but keep it up, its worth it. Once you get to the top, you have two options. 1. Enjoy the view and go down again, or 2. Go down the other side of the mountain for 40-45 metres and climb up another bump, for another great view. If you decide to go with number 2, then be sure to have a good pair of shoes on, two free hands to grab onto things so you don't fall. As said before, we are not climbers, and we managed to do the climb. Just be careful. The view is outstanding. I would prefer to go there in the morning, as the afternoon can be too hot for a climb. Bring water:)

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The hike to the top of little Adam's Peak is relatively short and very pleasent. The path is clear and you don't need any guides for this hike. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Quite easy to find, as there is a clear cut path.  the entrance is about 2Km from the Ella town and you can certainly walk it. It will take roughly 45 mins to get to the peak. The climb is quite easy and the last part of the ascend is through steps. The peak offers you a 360 degree view of the various beautiful mountain ranges and it is best to climb early morning to see the sun rise or in the evening around 5.30 to see the sunset. There is another peak which calls for a little more adventure if you dare to go down a quite steep descend and a equally grueling ascend.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: You do not need to be an expert climber or a trekking enthusiast to enjoy the Ella Gap from Little Adam's Peak. Most of the climb is by steps and only the last part you have to be a little careful but nothing which cannot be overcome by paying a normal digree of common sense and attention. There are 4 peaks in total but for your own safety I would stick with only the first two. Definetely worth the small effort.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a perfect walk for those who don't want to or cannot do the main Adam's peak or Ella rock. It is easy to find. Majority of the walk is on the road. The 360 view of the Ella town is beautiful. The walk itself is through tea plantations which is nice.

review_text: We had a couple of hours in the morning and decided to climb up Little Adam's peak with our children, ages 16, 13 and 8. It was a very good walk with easy trails passing by tea plantations and forest in some places. Some parts had paved steps which are quite steep but not a problem for our children. A few of the older visitors had to take frequent stops to catch their breath. There are quite a number of stray dogs on the trail but they seemed harmless. At the top of Little Adam's peak, the view is stunning. The walk down is much easier. We encountered some locals peddling local handicraft, tuk tuk services and king coconuts but at no point did we feel threatened. By the time we finished it was around 10am and we noticed a lot more visitors starting the trail then. Best to do it early like we did to avoid the crowds at the top of Little Adam's peak.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The climb to Little Adam's Peak is a short climb starting from the 98 Acres Resort. It takes about 20 minutes or so to get to the summit. The hike is relatively easy with concrete steps for the first two thirds and then becomes a rough pathway that is easy, if taken steadily. The summit offers multiple photo vantage points with 360 degree views of the tea plantations, mountains and valleys. There is a second summit that is a little more difficult due to the steepness and lack of clear footholds, but still do-able if taken steadily and wearing appropriate shoes (ie, not thongs or sandals). If climbing with children, I would keep a very close eye as there are no fences and the steep slopes would see a quick trip to the bottom! The jelly legs on the way down were worth the great view from the top!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We flew up and down Little Adam's Peak in 45mins, the view was amazing but myself and my husband looked at each other and said is that it... not much of a hike. IF YOU TAKE THE STAIRS; it's very do able in a pair of flip flops and would be a 4/10 in terms of fitness and ability, as there are plenty of places to stop as you walk up. BUT IF YOU ARE FIT AND USED TO WALKING AND DON'T MIND AN OBSTACLES OR TWO GO LEFT; go left when the stairs start and take the 25 min walk up the zig zag path. There were a times it looked like the path ended but it was just over grown bushes, get past this and your path will show again. The last 20m of the climb was tricky, as it was stepping up on to a big rock, (which could be hard if you don't have a strong core) and stepping through over grown bushes. It's not hard though as I dropped a t-shirt on the climb and did these last 20m again. At these last 20m you can see the top and hear people so it's worth just pushing through the over growth. 6/10 fitness and ability Taking the left after the very easy climb of the stairs made us feel like we deserved the view! We took the stairs back down, we were a little tired by this point. Take sun cream and wear good shoes if going left. No water sellers so bring you're own. Take money with you there is a nice Hotel you can stop at after the climb.

review_text: The best thing you can do is set off early in the morning, and you will meet some women going to work to tea plantations. By the time we reached the top, the only thing we could see was the mist, so we didn´t enjoy the view, but the climb was very pleasant anyway. There is a tea factory nearby, where you can see the process of making the tea,a s well as taste some.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Its an easy hike through a tea plantation to get to the top of the mountain. There are steps part if the way. We took the sandy foot path for the climb and took the stairs coming down. Its so beatiful when you get to the top. Great views all round.

review_text: We really enjoyed climbing little Adams peak. Firstly walking through the tea fields on the way to the main track was a highlight and then once on the main track, whilst the climb is a little strenuous, you can certainly take your time. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A semi-strenuous walk up to the top of little Adam's Peak. My wife and I had just come from climbing Big Adam's Peak a few days before so our legs were a bit more wobbly then usual! location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point

You can start by taking the road up next to the Flower Garden Resort and then finish by taking the other route back to 98 Acres.

review_text: From where our driver stopped us on the road, it’s just a short 30mins or so walk up to Little Adam’s Peak. It’s generally an easy hike with only slightly steep inclines in small sections. You get a nice scenic view of the surrounding mountains and and tea plantations at the top. All in, it’s a great way to spend 2 hours to get some great scenery without having to put in too much effort.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked to little Adams peak in April. It is the most beautiful place on Sri Lanka. A place you must see, when coming to Ella. We took a million pictures. Don't take the stairs up, but take the road up, and the stairs down. We highly recommend this trip

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A steady 45 minute walk to the top.  A mixture of rough pathways and concrete steps with fantastic views along the way.  If you visited The Rawana Ella falls on the way to Ella, you'll see them in the distance from the peak.  Worth a visit for the views and the breeze.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This walk takes around an hour or so and takes you through a beautiful tea plantation.  We had a 6year old and 12year old with us, neither had any difficulty with it although we did the walk early in the morning whilst it was relatively cool, any later and it may be too hot.  The route is well defined although there are 300 plus steps involved so beware if you do have any mobility issues.  The views from the top are incredible though so more than worth the effort !  We stopped on the way back at the garden cafe which was lovely and again set in a serene location with magnificent views.  Lots of animals (sadly in cages) to entertain the kids for half an hour ! Overall, worth the effort.

review_text: Some steep edges but generally seemed pretty safe. We finished the hike with an iced tea on the terrace at 98 acres (I think that's it's name). The tea came from the estate you walk through in your way to little Adams peek and the views are breathtaking.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Walked up this with three small children (youngest aged 5).  It only took about 40 minutes to get to the top, most of which is on a wide track with about ten minutes of steps at the top. Do be slightly careful on the steps because, despite walking up mid-morning when there were already a lot of people going both ways, my kids came across a cobra on a narrow part of the steps (which they were thrilled about).  Views from the top are awesome. 98 Acres is about ten minutes from the start/finish on the way to/from the peak.  It has an amazing setting but the food and staff are fairly unimpressive.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a relatively easy walk, which winds its way up to the top of Little Adam's Peak. Good path all the way up. I walked up in Birkenstocks so it's not at all bad underfoot. 98 Acres is a great spot for refreshment on the way down.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is in the top five of peaks in Sri Lanka if we remember our guide correctly. On the way to the peak you pass 98 Acres tea plantation and hotel (where you can arrive in your helicopter if you are so equipped). We blew past the helipad headed towards the peak, climbed about a thousand steps (well it seemed like a thousand) and then arrived at the peak and were treated to some really fabulous views. All in all it was less than an hour round-trip. Good fun!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This walk is only about 45 minutes each way for reasonably fit people ( we are nearly 70 and had no trouble) but it is quite steep and it would be very exhausting in the heat of the day. Do stop and look at the hand made gift stall just after the gate as you turn right on the track before the real climb begins. It is run by a delightful young lady and her mother who make the items themselves. Nice stuff and fair prices with no pressure  (unusual in Sri Lanka). Take water and drink it whilst enjoying the panoramic view from the summit.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a great little walk for the family. The path is clearly marked and wide, the steps are a little steep towards the end but even I with my very unfit and rather fat body managed to get up there with not much effort. There's even a geocache/earth cache to be gained at the top. We stopped off at the 98 acres on the way down for a little rest and a drink. I would go early morning, we went at 10 and the weather was fine.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: ***It's not exactly climbing Mount Everest but do not wear flip flops there is a lot of dirt track which you will slip on so don't be stupid** Lovely view of the local area really stunning! If you're as white as I am you'll need good sun protection on. Views of the tea plantation, tea pickers along the way. When you come back down the hill have a walk to the green tea factory also.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Do it in the evening or morning when the light is pretty. It's really just a short walk from Ella and a very modest ascent in the end for a great view of the valley. You'll pass through some tea fields on the way, really scenic and well worth it.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A nice hike.  Easy to do.  Take a rain coat in case it rains as there is no shelter. A bottle of water will be helpful as well. Proper shoes for walking and climbing an asset. The view is phenomenal.  Totally worth the 30 minute walk. If you get hungry or in need of a coffee fix...  You can visit '98 acres'  hotel cafe.  Excellent views from there with super friendly service.  I have attached photos from both: little Adams peak and 98acres

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Great short walk. Really gives you good views of Ella, and the surrounding landscape. Not a difficult walk technically as there are steps, when it gets steep. On the way up or down, would highly recommend having a drink or lunch at 98 degrees. It was our favourite lunch location - just beautiful.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I'm fairly fit but far from naturally athletic (lol) but managed the walk easily in the morning when it was a little cooler, its a mainly flat route up until the steps, then you're at the top rewarded by great views! Allow 1-2 hours, take a brolly to shade yourself if you go between 12-3pm. We had a snack and tea at the fab Adams Breeze restaurant when we climbed down, and then continued to the Nine Arch Bridge, headed down the shortcut at the viewpoint (VERY steep) and walked back to Ella via the train tracks - a great way to round off Little Adams Peak!

Sunset is around 6pm, and even if there is some people around, is a peaceful and beautiful place to see the mountains around Ella

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We really enjoyed this hike. Took us about 1 hour and 15 minutes including stopping to take in the view and photos. Be ware of the local with snakes. My boyfriend wanted photos and he then asked for 1000 rupees. We said no and gave him 400.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We really enjoyed our walk to Little Adams Peak. At our start, still in Ella, we were lucky to see a wedding on the way with dances and beautiful dresses.Then we walked through tee plantations and saw the first tea pickers, some wanted to be photographed hoping to get a tip. We stopped for a coffee at "Cafe 98"in "The 98 Acres" hotel ,what a fantastic place !! the perfect combination of comfort and nature.We just did not want to leave and ordered some drinks and french fries. Outside they have two tables with sun umbrellas the view is great,nearby is a small pool for hotel guests only. Inside the Restaurant is very nice and you will be very thankful for the A/C. After this perfect stop we continued our excursion to Little Adams Peak.The last minutes climbing to the peak are not difficult but quite tiring because of the heat, later we saw that we had taken a short cut and some other tourists were walking another way expecting to be easier, but in any case you will enjoy a fantastic view  under a tree with a nice breeze.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We started around 5pm, you could go up to the gate either in a Tuk Tuk or a scooter or simply walk all the way. From the gates it's just a 30 minutes climb with less than 70-80 stairs at the last. If you miss the sunset, you miss out on the best part. During noon the view is gazed hence not the best. But during sunset this is heaven. We stayed seated on the rock until the complete sun set. You can get back easily before dark. MUST TRY!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We set off to climb little Adam's peak around 4pm on a weekend. It is short walk (15 mins) from the town and you enter a tea estate. The path to little Adam's peak is through this estate. It's a lovely walk, especially in the late afternoon. Once you climb up, there are 3 peaks that you can trek towards. All 3 offer lovely views. We waited until the sun went down and it was magical. On your way back, do walk past 98 acres, a fancy resort. The property is beautiful and you can enjoy a cup of tea or a beer there. They also offer foot massages. Little Adam's peak is worth the trek and I'd do it again on my next trip to Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Brilliant views! Wear comfortable shoes, take water, hat etc. There are 3 peaks which you can climb, the first 2 are directly next to each other, and the 3rd is a little further and harder to get to as involves going down and back up - but it's worth the effort.  Go early morning as it will get hot and if you go before tu Rose take a torch! There is a stray dog that might walk with you, but he is friendly - we took some food and water for him when we went :)

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Only a short walk from Ella town, this is well worth the effort! Great views from the top of the surrounding mountain ranges and tea plantations. You should walk to the adjacent peak from the view point for the best view (turn right at the top of the steps for the standard viewpoint, turn left and follow the downtrodden grass/trail path for a better view). This was so much better than the real Adam's Peak!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We enjoyed this relaxing walk very much, it is about a half hour (or 45 minutes) walk to the summit from the centre of Ella. The walk is not difficult and can be done by almost everybody who is not crippled I think. You have actually 3 peaks two are easy to reach and the one at the end is much more difficult to reach. The way to the last peak has at first a steep descent en after that a steep climb (and you have to come the same way back). But the view from the last peak is by far the best, although the views are from all the 3 peaks are wonderful. On the way back we stopped for a drink at the wonderful 98 Acres Resort (which is situated on the route) and this is a very refreshing after the beautiful walk in the heat.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is definitely worth the trek. Depending on your physical condition, it'll take you somewhere between 30 minutes or more to reach the top. My friend and I did it in about 40 minutes, just walking and enjoying the ascend on the path. Reaching the top requires you to go through lots of stairs, so be ready for that. Also, at some point there was a "blockade" for the path leading up towards Little Adam's Peak, which confused us a bit, but you just go "through/under" it, no worries. The reward is an amazing view over the mountains around Ella. It'd recommend everyone to do it if you're around and got a pair of working legs.

review_text: Spent a couple of days in Ella to climb Little Adam's Peak and go to the Nine Arches Bridge. Also took the train from Hatton to Ella. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We took a tuk tuk from ella (Buses are also available)  and ride 3 km from Ella to reach the entrance. From there, we hike across tea estate and climbed the mountain. Dont forget to bring your raincoats , because it might rain at anytime. There are plenty of places to take photos, and i highly recommend to take photos at " 98 acres" ' s Helipad, which is located near the trail. We enjoyed the "Coco passion" drink also.  The whole tour can  be covered within 2 hours, if you are a average climber. The total cost including travelling expenses and drinks from Ella would be less than LKR 2000 for a couple.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We woke up early and climbed the hill before 6 am, so that we can see the sun rise. It is an easy walk, 45-90 minutes (depending on where your guest house is located) to the top. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My husband and I climbed this peak starting at around 9am. The start of the path is concreted and the trail easy going. After around 700m the path splits in two. To the left you can continue on the trails or to the right there are the stairs. 425 of them, I counted on my way down. There are several meandering tracks up the peak. All eventually leading to the top. I recommend the tracks up and the stairs down. Wear good shoes. Either a sturdy trainer or walking shoes. Don't do this in flip flops. Also wear long trousers as there is a lot of vegetation some a little sharp/thorny. There can also be snakes. Take water too. The ascent took us around 40 minutes up the track, a steady easy going pace. The track gets a little craggy in places and there are a few loose rocks and large steps but nothing requiring any high level of fitness. The views from the top are stunning. We took the stairs back down. Descending in around 20 minutes. So it's a relatively short walk. I don't recommend going up the stairs unless you're incredibly fit with a good set of knees!

review_text: We really enjoyed waking up little adams peak. It's quite a scenic walk and very accessible for people of all ages. Loads of tourists from 5-70 years old were heading up there when we went, and most people were managing it in flip flops. You could even get a tuk tuk halfway up if you were not inclined to walk. Some locals suggested we should go at 5am to catch the sunrise but i don't think it's really necessary. We went around 9am and it was fine,  but it got really hot and there wasn't much shade so I'd recommend sunscreen and a bottle of water. The view along the way is pretty as you go through some tea fields and the view at the top is spectacular so take a camera. I'm afraid of heights so i didn't make the trek from one of the summits to the next point but the first summit is easy enough to reach and you can get great photos from there. There are some locals on the walk that will pose for photos for money and we saw a snake charmer as well but mainly it was just tourists.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We visited little Adams peak this morning - it's easy to find and we managed without a guide. There are beautiful views of the tea plantations as you approach and then stunning views of Ella rock and surrounding area from the peak. We started from Pasana road in town (the main Street) and at the junction there's a huge sign for 98 acres hotel. Follow that. Keep walking up the road for 30 mins or so past all the guest houses and you'll soon see the sign for Little Adams peak. Once you've walked through the plantations the road comes to a Y shape. Take the left path. Easy! You'll see plenty of other tourists to ask as well. Or look on google maps as we did. There were some tuktuk drivers at the bottom who tried to tell us they could take us to the summit via a road or we'd have to climb 5000 steps.... There's only about 500 or less steps so it was fine & you can stop to admire the view along the way. A lovely way to spend the morning. We were fine wearing flip flops but you'd need proper walking shoes if it had rained. Visit the small cafe for delicious coco pineapple juice on the way up or down! Owned by a super friendly & chatty Sri Lankan chap.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We wanted to hike the Ella Rock but since we didn't have enough time, we choose this place. Heard very little of it so I was not expecting to see something amazing because a lot of tourists are going there and the roads were concreted and wide. As a native Sri Lankan, I've had enough experiences with walking along tea estates. BUT I WAS WRONG! And, I'm glad I was wrong. So the story goes like this. We went to the car park, which was empty. There was this friendly old man who told us how far is it and stuff. He said, its just a 1km hike to the top. So I thought, I can make the 1km in 30 mins tops. So I left everything (my backpack, shoes, umbrella) in the car and started walking along the road to the top. Did not think for a second that it would rain. Along the way, (btw you can get to 98 acres resort from this road) through tea plantations, I stumbled upon a guava tree. Why waste precious fruit, I plucked a few, ate along the way. Passed the gate and walked along the road passing 98 acres helipad. Once I came to the junction, a local tour guide told us that we can either take the stairs to the top or we can take the path through the jungle. We choose that,  for like 100m it was wide enough and then It was just a foot path. Apparently no one seem to take that path. Which is another reason to take that path instead of stairs. Nice views. Trust me. We go to the top. and someone told us there are 8 more summits. We took the challenge and visited all of them. After the 3rd, no one has set foot on the rest. The path was not clear. We made it there though. And it started raining.......heavily... So, don't forget your umbrella!. Visit all 8 summits. Be really careful.  The views are amazing. Some suggestions: >> After the 3rd summit, pathways aren't clear. You should find a strong stick or something to clear out the way. Please don't bring knifes to cut down the bushes. Protect the environment. >> There are rocks extruding out of the mountain and you can sit on them. Be careful. Don't be scared. >> If it started raining, pathway gets very slippery. >> There is no shelter. >> You can see the distant lands if you go betweek 12:00pm - 3:00pm as there is no mist cover. >> Have fun!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My boyfriend and I walked up to Little Adam's Peak yesterday afternoon - we're not regular walkers but didn't find it difficult at all. The walk consisted of an uphill amble through tea plantations, past tethered cows, the cobra man and a lady selling wonderful, natural seed jewellery. The final 20% is up a mixture of steps and steepish path but I'm honestly not fit at all, with a historic knee injury and coped just fine. From the top the views were incredible. Take the right at the top and you'll see the 'official', flagged summit and the left is worth a wander too for slightly different views. Just a quick note, when we took the left turn there was a stray hanging around. He had mange on his back end, his tail between his legs and looked very dejected and hot. Unfortunately, I didn't have any food on me at all but made a bowl out of my hands and offered him our water. He was nervous at first but in the end, lapped up our whole bottle. He was honestly incredibly sweet, I even gave him a little scrub on the head and he closed his eyes and had a happy moment. If you go up there in the next few days, please please take some food/water/a bit of love. Enjoy!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We left close to 9am for Little Adam's Peak. To be honest, before we went, I was really afraid of leeches. Thank god we encountered none. The weather held up, it was a bright sunny day. The walk from our hotel (We were staying at Ravana Heights) to the top of Little Adam's Peak took us about an hour. You walk amongst the tea plantations and will see the tea pickers at work. It is a lovely sight, do smile at them and ask before you take a photo, it is only polite. You will encounter a snake charmer on your way, we didn't engage with him as I am terrified of snakes. I have read that the cobras are heavily drugged so that they perform. It is a photo opportunity if you are keen, the snake charmer and his cobra, though I have read from other reviews that they didn't have a pleasant experience with him. Most of the way is paved and it has steps. It becomes a dirt path for the last 10 mins of the climb up. We went on a sunny day, though I reckon it would be slippery, post rain. It is beautiful on the top, it has three viewing points and offers a 360 view. And of course, lots of photo taking opportunities. A common photo would be to sit on a rock jutting out with the landscape behind, it is an unobstructed view so it makes a pretty picture. When you reach the top, you can access two of the viewing points easily, the third is a steep climb down and up. The third one gives you a view of the misty hills. We did all three, though the third one required the full use of my hands and feet to get through. It is worth the climb, and you don't have to be very fit to do it, just pace yourself and you will be fine. Wear sunscreen and bring plenty of water. I would recommend covered shoes and to go early (Leave your hotel around 7am) to avoid the heat and the people. Some people recommend getting there before the sunrise, so you might want to do that.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The road to Little Adam's Peak is just a short stroll from Ella Town. I went early in the morning and the weather was nice and brisk, if a bit overcast. The trail was well-worn and a fairly easy hike with steep stairs as I approached the summit. By the time I got to the top, most of the clouds and mist had burned off, offering a breathtaking view of mountaintops as far as the eye could see. If you take the shortcut to Demodara Nine Arch (Nine Arch Bridge) from Little Adam's Peak, beware of leeches, especially if it rains the night before.

We missed the turn and ended up having to go through a hotel (98 something) 2km further up the road...which wasn't a big deal. Make no mistake, you will work up a sweat getting there but from town, the whole walk took us about 45mins (including the long way up). We stayed at Waterfalls guest house and if you go towards that, near Zion guest house there is a lookout next to the rd which I actually think has a better view. You can see Ella rock, the waterfall and the valley all in one shot.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We took a tuktuk to Garden View Restaurant where the track starts. The first part of the walk went through tea plantations with nice sourroundings. The last part to the peak was up some steep stairs. But it went well. Even our children, 5 and 7 enjoyed the 35 mins. walk to the peak. The view from the top is very nice and well worth the effort. Afterwards we enjoyed a well deserved lunch at the Garden View Restaurant. Good food and great view!

review_text: We enjoyed this, even in the rain. It's a great little hike and at the very top, as you turn left, there's a sad looking small dog with mange. We visited the local vets but the clinic for dogs is only from 8am to 10am and we were departing before that the next day. Mange is not fatal but it's a pretty miserable, itchy Life and very treatable. If you see this dog the vet treatment is less than £25 and I'm happy to compensate you for your time and effort. Find me via FB. The vets is on the walk from town to little adams peak. There's a piece of rope at the top of the hill to use as a lead.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is an easy walk with signs telling you where to walk. It's starts easy through beautiful tea-plantations, before it gets a bit heavier reaching to the top. This is a good trip to combine with the "9 arch bridge", which is in the same area.

review_text: Way of climbing is similar to the Adam's peak but in small scale. At the top you'll have view of 360 degrees. On one side you can see the Wellawaya - Badulla main road. That's the Ella pass. One of the five passes to Central highlands of Sri Lanka. It is a place to have a nice view of a pass. The climbing will take one hour for an average person. To get there, use the 98 acres path from Ella - Passara road. There's another route but with no vehicle access. Only footpath. If you go by public transport, get the Namunukula bus from Ella and buy tickets to "Punchi Sri Padaya"

review_text: This is a nice walk through the local yes plantation. Once at the top there are spectacular views. It's very easy to find from town and can be done without a Guide. I would recommend good shoes because we seen snakes, and the trail is uneven with sometimes sharp granite rock.  Water and food is available on the way and also a nice spice tour.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A nice, easy walk up to the peak with tea plantations all around. Good views of the surrounding countryside once you get to the top. Stop off at the 98 Acres resort for a drink and a look at what a luxury resort is like on the way, and on your way back you can go by way of the 9 Arches Bridge (once you get back onto the main road by the Flower Garden Resort, head right for about 800 metres then follow signs for the 9 Arch Lodge; keep going down past the lodge on a track that gets smaller and smaller, crosses a creek then finally ends up on the railway tracks by the bridge.) You can then walk along the railway tracks back to Ella (watching out for oncoming trains obviously...)

review_text: Go on a sunny day and the short climb will yield you stunning view of Ella's Rock! location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Before our visit to Ella, we read numerous comments on this climb and decided we'll hike up as well. I was apprehensive in the beginning as I am NOT an athletic person and I couldn't even remember when was my last hike up anywhere. Therefore if a non-atheletic city folk like me made it to the top, anyone can do it. We read about the 2 ways climb up the peak in a forum when you arrive at the steps. We decided to take the trail up on the left instead of the steps. Halfway through, we thought we were lost a couple of times as the path seemed to vanish into shrubs and tall grasses but we made it in the end. It is definitely a more interesting hike up the peak compared to taking the steps. The view is just magnificent. You have to do this.....

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is perfect to fit in if you have a more busy program. It can be done in little over an hour and the view is just amazing. You can see for miles and miles and can even spot Ravana falls from the top. The walk is not too hard and is fitted with stairs so you won't be bathing in sweat. There are also plenty of trees so there is enough shadow if you want to do it during the afternoon when the sun is usually too hot for other heavy activities.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked up Little Adam's Peak whilst staying at 98 acres resort and spa. This is a great little walk, not too challenging and can easily be under an hour.  It is easy to access via steps and the view is well worth it. You can see for miles and miles, we also had binoculars which we borrowed from our hotel. We even managed to spot Ravana waterfall which we visited the following day. Very nice walk and great views, highly recommended

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Nothing compared to the real Adam's peak, though still a very enjoyable walk amongst a great scenery. On the way back, make sure you'll plan a stop at the 98 acres resort for a refreshing drink and further relaxing views on the gorgeous scenery.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Very easy to climb just make sure you wear a high sun cream factor! I had a factor 20 on and was still burnt to a cinder despite only being in the sun 9-11, the breeze can really mask the sun's intensity at that altitude. Make sure when you get to the summit you venture over to the left peak. It's a bit of a steep climb down and then up again, but takes less than 10mins and very worth it. It gets you away from the masses, the organised tours and the occasional 'delight' who wants to share their phone music with everyone, and allows you to just take in the beauty in peace and quiet.

review_text: A small hill situated above the town of Ella popular for it's 360 degree stunning views of the area. It is particularly popular for romantic sunrise and sunset visits.  The climb is relatively easy, mainly up concrete steps.  I had recently had a knee replacement and managed OK!  Nothing on top except views for Africa (!?) and some stray dogs.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: As I have extreme fear of heights, climbing Little Adam's Peak was somewhat of a daring enterprise. However, it turned out to be a very easy hike in lovely Ella hill country, with some challenging stairs at the end, but... nothing terrible. The views from the top are awesome. Really, really worth the effort (because it can get quite hot if you do not start early in the morning).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is a must do when visiting Ella. The climb takes about 30-45 mins each way and takes you through tea plantations and alongside the exclusive 98 Acres Resort. Not as challenging as Ella Rock so doable without a guide. You can take the steps up to the peak or the track road. We took our time once at the top to drink in the views. We went up in the morning as the weather was clear allowing for stunning views of Ella Rock opposite and the valley beneath.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Starting from the footpath turn-off beside the flower shop on Passara Road, it's a 45-minute stroll along a well-trodden path. The incline is so gentle, even children were skipping along. Only the last one-quarter of the walk (I won't even call it a hike) needed a little effort, consisting of about 330 steps in succession. But why should you hurry? At every step of the way, pause as much as you wish and enjoy the views. The lower reaches take you through tea gardens. Look beyond the bushes, and there are great views of Ella Rock across the valley. More distant views appear as you get higher, and finally, Little Adam's Peak rewards you with three humps. It's great fun getting your friends onto one hump while you scurry over to another to shoot a photo of them (a moderate telephoto lens will be required). Best to go between 7 and 9am, but it's still possible to do so later so long as you have a hat, sunblock and water. Not much exertion needed, yet you'll be rewarded with great views! The footpath turn-off is marked. It can be found beside the flower shop about 1.2km from Ella Village along Passara Road.

review_text: Little Adams Peak is part of a lovely circular walk from Ella that also takes in the Nine Arch Bridge and the Newburgh Tea Factory. In fact, once you leave the road out of Ella, the walk up to Little Adams Peak is through the Newburgh tea estate. I'd thoroughly recommend it, it's an all day walk but does take in some wonderful sights. The views from Little Adams Peak are stunning, and the green tea at the Newburgh Tea Factory is a treat. There are some nice places to stop in at for drinks or nibbles on the way. Just as you leave the Ella road and enter the tea estate, there's a small simple thatched place by the road called the Kashawi Restaurant that has a huge sign outside advertising COCO PASSION, which is a coconut, with added passionfruit juice or pineapple juice. Delicious and very refreshing!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We were desperate to get away from the dust and noise of Ella town and with a few hours until dinner time, the walk to little Adams peak seemed like the right thing to do. It's a well trodden tourist trail and we shared the paths and the views from the top with up to ten others at any given time. After meandering amongst tea bushes there are multiple pathways to the peak. We chose the straight-up-stairs way which was a bit daunting to me at times due to the steepness of them. I'm pleased I got over my vertigo because I'd have missed the most breathtaking views from the summit and the beer afterwards at 98 Acres would've felt far less deserved. I think every visitor to Ella should attempt this walk to get a sense of the true grandeur of the place. It makes you realise why people come here.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It's not far, a walking distance from ella, about 2 km. The way starts with the main road, and goes inside the tea plantations. It's a beautiful walk, and in the end there's a some what steep climb, though a short one. We did it with children aged 3-13 with no problem. The views from the peak are amazing, and it's a great place for a picnic and some relaxing time in the top . One can easily spend half a day there.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: From Ella flower garden resort it is only a 30 minute walk to the peak. It´s a very easy walk with only little difference of attitude (around 100 meters). Once there you will have a great view on the fantastic nature around. Very recommendable.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The view is amazing and the trek is pretty easy. About ten minutes away from Ella town. There are many trails on this hill so it's easy to get lost if there's no one around. That happened to me as I went on the wrong path and ended up bashing my way through the vegetation. There was an old trail so it wasn't too bad, but it could have been a lot easier. Make sure you go at a time when there are people! Many locals visit this attraction so you could follow them up. There's no need for a guide. There will be people touting for photos and trinkets along the way.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Was a good, easy to navigate walk which is great for me as I get lost going to my own bathroom Gorgeous views, so nice to be in amongst so much nature, really fresh air real tea leaf pickers at work. They say "photo?" And I was like wow I'm flattered, they want a photo of me but then I realised they wanted me to take a photo of them in exchange for some of my cash. I did it once but then I said no to the others and they were fine with it Do it, and wear good shoes

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I went on 2 consecutive days - 1st day around 10am in the morning, and then decided to come again on the 2nd day to catch the sunrise. The sunrise was good, except that there were some clouds, so it fell short of an excellent sunrise. Allow for an easy 1 hour walk from Ella town (normally 45 minutes), as it would be pitch dark. A torchlight is necessary and a Google map is useful. It is an easy walk, so no worries about your fitness level. You can easily make it back for a breakfast before catching the 9:20am train back to Colombo.

review_text: We climbed Little Adams peak during afternoon, as we didn't feel like waking up for sunrise.. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Nice easy walk from Ella along the Passara Road to the garden centre, through the garden centre and tea plantations.  It took us just under one hour from Ella’s Edge resort.  Very good views of Ella Rock and down into the lowlands.  We stopped for dinner at the 98 Acres Resort on the way back and had a great meal.  The sunset was incredible.  We then decided to return for sunrise and set out from Ella’s Edge by tuktuk at 430am.  It was quite cool on the top before sunrise but the views were spectacular as the sun rose over the plains and struck Ella Rock.  You will be joined by a pack of local dogs who are all friendly.  Definitely worth the hike and much shorter than Ella Rock.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A lot of people in our group found this hike more strenuous than Ella Rock because of the amount of steep steps, although the actual distance is much less. And the hike itself is not as varied or beautiful as Ella Rock. Nevertheless, the view at the top is worth it! Beware the children en route who ask you for 'pens for school' Take enough water. Only 3 of us in a group of 10 carried water. 😐 Climb the other hills connected to Little Adam's Peak for an extended and more satisfactory hike. There's a nice spot to have breakfast among the tall grasses. Climb this as a starter, and do Ella Rock the next day.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's peak is a nice walk, but yuo will need to get up early. Start the walk between 7-8 at the entrance of the park, so you are there before the clouds come ( around 11). Don't forget that the road to the park is long, so you will need to get up around early. When you enter the park you will probably see some deers. Don't forget to avoid all plastic bags, since they will be removed by security when you enter. Even the package around my crackers had to go, same as the plastic around my water bottle. The walk is very nice, but you preferably wear some decent shoes since you have some " off road" conditions. If you do the complete tour ( small world's end, worlds end and the waterfall) it will take you 3 hours on a decent speed.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The path up to Little Adam's Peak is mostly a road, a bit rough for a vehicle but easy walking. (There is a community up there, which is why there's a road.) The clim was a steady incline, so pacing yourself it's not too strenuous. Once the trail leaves the road the path is narrower, of course, and becomes steeper. Then you hit the stairs- a passing woman had counted over two hundred stairs, she told us with a grin, and we weren't at the top yet. Beware, it will make your thighs ache. But once you've navigated that, it becomes easy again. The view from the peak is stunning, as one would expect. There was a cool wind blowing steadily, and several vantage points allow you to get a 360 degree view. Coming down you will pass by the 98 Acres Resort. They have a cafe there which we can highly recommend, with good food and beer for a hiker cooling down after a climb. Another excellent view with beanbag chairs available. I found myself wishing that there were places like that in all of the places I've gone hiking- I would hike more, but probably gain weight in the process. Overall an excellent experience, hiking through the tea plantation to a very pleasant area with a magnificent viewpoint. What's not to love about it?

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A not too difficult hike will take you up to the peak which is centrsl to lots of valleys in the area and so commands some pretty spectacular views all around, once the clouds clear! Although we walked up in the rain and were initially surrounded by cloud, a gentle breeze did clear it away and we got a great experience of watching the hills around us appear from within the mist and the feeling of being above the cloud swirling in the valleys below. Fab.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My husband and I left our place around 530am when it was just light (no torch required) and walked the pleasant 45min from our accommodation to the top. Temperature was very comfortable compared to going later in the day and there were few people. We struck a handful of people coming down who had obviously gone earlier to see the first light but that would have meant walking in the dark which wasn't really us. Other than that we seemed to be alone bar a few tuk tuks who were ferrying the locals around and a couple of stray but friendly dogs who took it upon themselves to guide us to the top (It seems there are a couple of pairs of dogs who do this though and get a bit territorial when they cross paths). Beautiful scenery once you hit the dirt path through the tea plantation. Got to the top by climbing the steps (although the path that winds around to the left will get you to the top too as that's how we came down). We didn't make it in time for sunrise but the views were spectacular. Well worth it - especially if you get up early!

review_text: This is a really pleasant walk from Ella , lots to see on the way , with a few strenuous parts towards the top. But the view is well worth it . review_text: Ella it self is a beautiful town the   views from the hotel rooms  amazing, the scenery , the sunset and the sunrise are awesome , climbing little Adam peak is other thing which must to do, your bag should be  light,carry  water, hat and wear good thick sole shoe that  give you advantage in hiking. their is a young man at the start of the track who sell some ornaments made of jungle seeds in their natural colors worth buying, if you are in no  hurry the round trip can be done within two hours..go and enjoy it .

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak is the beautiful mountain of about 1141 metres. It's a good stroll, wasn't too hard, but i'd recommend wearing proper footwear (sneakers or so) instead of flipflops like some people were. Our guesthouse The Chillout is located right at the start of the walking path towards Little Adams Peak. When you are staying in the mainstreet you'd better take a tuktuk to the start of the trail, or you'll find yourself walking at least 20 minutes uphill just to reach the start of the path. Tuktuks should charge no more than 150 rupees for this ride. While climbing the peak, you'll notice there are something more than 1 road towards the top. Most of the time both roads will get you there, but one might be with many steps, the other way is a flat road going uphill (so easier) but much longer. Everybody recommends starting early, well i guess that is true. It might get hot during the afternoon, but for us coming down in the heat wasn't that terrible. Beats getting up everyday at 5 or 6 to be back before the heat... When coming down, you can stop at the 98 acres resort. It's a beautifull luxurious place located in the midst of teaplantations. The owners of the hotel actually own the teaplantions around. Though luxurious, the hotel welcomes everyone walking Little Adam's Peak to stop and freshen up. You can have a drink while sitting in beanbags enjoying the fantastic view. Lunch was good too. Try to follow the path to 98 acres that starts just next to the path with the big metal barrier. If you look at the barrier, the other path to 98 acres is located left. This is a flat road where cars and tuktuks drive. When you head on to the peak (barrier-road) you will see a sign for 98 acres to your left at sometime, but this road is a bit more tricky... Enjoy your walk!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy walk either from 98 acres resort or from the road from Ella. Great views fromm the top. Walk through tea plantation. Top tip - if you want to avoid the steps to the summit just follow the pathetic to the left at the start of them. This will take you to the top on a more gentle and pleasant ascent.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Some narrow steps and uneven ground as you get close to top, wear good shoes... seen people in flip flops struggling......bring small change, there is a small hut serving water and sodas halfway there but he does little business so has no change... nice guy. A welcome drink on the way down...

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Well for this guy in his mid 70's it was a great sense of achievement to reach the summit of Little Adam's Peak.  It was a really enjoyable walk/climb...I wish I had counted the number of steps but I'm sure someone has! I think it's best to do it early in the day before it gets too hot.  The views from the top are quite stunning.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I didn't know about this hike until my guesthouse mentioned it to me. Its a shorter (less confusing) hike than the one to Ella rock and in my opinion a much nicer one. Won't take you more than 90mins return from trailhead unless you decide to picnic at the top. The views as you walk along the spine of this big hill are just amazing, Bring long pants as you will be hiking through some bushes. The main path is an easy trek but you can choose to continue on a much less defined path and get away from the other hikers if you want. (Even that path really isn't terrible even for people who don't hike much). I highly recommend this hike!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Even if you are not a hiker and it gets very steep at few locations, there are stairs leading to the top and you can reach it also with small children. Especially if you are not a hiker, you get a pure joy of reaching the top and get the views. Worth a try.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: After visiting Horton's the day before this was quite a short hike and relatively easy, at least for the first part.  Unfortunately it was rainy and foggy so didn't really see the view at its best but it was still worth the effort - we took a different way down through the tea plantations and this was interesting as came very close to the tea pickers. Not for the less able and wear decent walking shoes.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: One of the best things to see/do in Sri Lanka. Don't forget to hike there even if you don't feel like going until the top and exploring other peaks around. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Few things are free in Sri Lanka, in fact this is the only activity we did during our 3 weeks that was free. So since it's free, go ahead and do it! review_text: This was a great little hike that requires just basic fitness and balance. The roads and steps leading to the top are mostly paved except for a short strip toward the end. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A lovely walk, and one of the highlights of our stay in the sleepy little village that is Ella. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We had a great walk today to Little Adam's Peak. I carried our 4 year old on my shoulders most of the way and enjoyed the hike which was very easy except for some steps at the end. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: In order to get there the best way is to take a tuk-tuk or drive to the 98 acres hotel car park. From there its a concrete trek that takes 30 min to 1 hour to get to the top. Do not attempt the trek on a rainy day or a day where it is extremely foggy and mist because the steps will be slippery and you wont be able to see anything. On your way back down you can stop at the 98 acres hotel restaurant and have a hot cup of fresh tea or a cool glass of beer. There are no leaches and the view from the top is simply amazing!! A trip to Ella is not complete without this.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This is an easy walk (sauntering perhaps an hour to the top from the main street in Ella), partly along the road and then up a sandy trail, through a tea plantation and then finally steps to the top. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I had done this climb the day after I had done Ravana cave and Ella rock so I was a little tired. I felt this climb was a little harder than Ella rock. The entrance to this rock is through a tea garden so that was nice. There are two major peaks. The first one is easier. The second one was harder. I had to climb using both my hands and feet. The last part required walking over a short path which overlooked the edge of the cliff. So I had to stop there as it was already evening and I was very tired. Overall, it was a quiet and serene place to be in. I do want to go back there to complete the second peak. The owners of the small restaurant at the entrance were really friendly. I would highly recommend getting a king coconut there on the way back.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: If you don't have long in Ella or don't fancy the steep walk up Ella Rock then definitely visit Little Adam's Peak. On the way down there are a number of signs to the 98 Acres Resort, where you can stop for a drink in luxurious surroundings before heading back to the town.

review_text: When you get to the top this is actually a very good viewpoint and the ascent is very straightforward. review_text: We visited little Adams peak when staying at the nearby 98 acres resort. It was an hours round trip from the resort. We kind of fell on the path after breakfast so I was in flip flops as oppose to walking shoes and this wasn't a problem. The paths were good and an easy walk, followed by steps up to the peak. There were a fair few steps to the top plus a little uneven surface near the top, but manageable even in flip flops, and the views at the top when you reach the white flag were very rewarding. We could see valley and surrounding waterfalls. Stunning views. We weren't sure we could be bothered to do the walk originally (being pulled by the pool and spa) but were glad we did when we saw the views on route and at the top, definitely worth taking out a few hours to complete it.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: About one hour return walk from town. Went up early for sunrise, great view, got some nice photos. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I had the company of 2 new friends that I met at my hotel. Initially, I felt worried about hiking on my own but there were many tourists climbing as well. I would've been fine even on my own. Getting to the foot of Little Adam's Peak can be a little unclear (about 15 minutes walk from town) but you can ask anyone along the way for directions. It's unlikely that you'd get lost though. The walk up wasn't too tough. The slightly steep steps got to me a little because we were going pretty fast. We reached the peak in about 35 minutes. The view of the tea plantation going up was nice and the weather was pleasant. A tea leaf picker offered to let us take a photo of her but we politely declined (in case she wanted to be paid for taking her photo). The peak gives you a perfect view down the Ella Gap and Ella Rock. It's the perfect spot for spectacular photos. You'd be tempted to sit on the rocks but please do be very very careful because it can be windy up there. Overall, a great experience and Ella is truly one of the most beautiful places in Sri Lanka. I can't wait to go again! :)

review_text: You will need to be in reasonable physical shape to be able to complete the climb up to Little Adams Peak. However, once you get to the top the views are superb.
