location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A nice nature walk, through tea plantations, on an easy to navigate path. It's not really a trek, so if you are a hardcore a athletic outdoorsy type, you might find this a bit tame. For us though, it was a nice easy way to spend a few hours, filming the tea plantations, and looking across Ella Gap. The last section up to the top of the Peak is via a lot of concrete steps. So if your knees can't take steps, you may not like the last little section. But you could still do the majority, first part. Big, white golf flag at the top. Can't miss it. On the way back, you could drop into the newish 98 Acres Resort. (Hotel and chalets perched right on the cliff edge) They have a cafe looking into the yonder. It was absolutely empty when we were there. So this resort is either struggling, or everybody was hiding. It also has a pool, but I can't help thinking the climate is a bit cool for that, up in the hills.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Not a steep or difficult hike, but an enjoyable one. An elderly lady kept asking us to take her picture as she picked tea leaves at the side of the trail (it runs through a tea plantation). We imagined a tip to be involved and declined her offer. We spotted a couple of places to stop for drinks or snacks on the way. The view is fantastic from the top. Quick tip for those as foolish as myself - when you're nearing the top, you'll come to a stone staircase. It is not anyone's private property. It leads to the top and will get you there in 5 minutes or less. If you do not take this staircase, you will zig-zag back and forth through a grassy wilderness for about 20 minutes until you reach the top the old fashioned way. Either way, it was a good way to spend the morning. Surprisingly, no guides offered their services to us at the bottom. If you are not so fortunate, be advised that this is not a complex labyrinth of trails that requires someone to lead you. You go up. And there are signs (but again, take the stairs near the top).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A beautiful hike up to Little Adams Peak through the tea plantations. There are a few ways up and we took the easiest option which was quite a nice stroll. it was very hot and humid. Part way up there is a tiny little shack selling juices which is well worth a stop! If only we had know to stop on the way up as well as on the way back! The fresh fruit juices sold here are amazing and, we believe, the best we tasted in Sri Lanka! The photo opportunity at the top of the Peak is well worth the climb and there is a rock sticking out at the top that you can perch on (although not for those with a fear of heights). A lovely morning stroll.

review_text: We started the hike at around 9am and it was already getting hot by this time so would recommend starting as early as possible.  The route was pleasant with some fantastic views along the way so you will find yourself stopping for photos of the stunning scenery!  Although we had heard the path was supposedly clearly marked we somehow managed to get a little lost on the way up!  We ended up scrambling which I had not read about previously so a quick scout around led us back to the correct route up the steps.  The steps were a little challenging in the heat otherwise I would say anyone with a reasonable level of fitness would be fine with this.  The views at the top were well worth the hike! It was extremely peaceful with amazing 360 degree views.  We took the other route down via 98 acres resort which was actually much easier than taking the steps up.  Would definitely suggest to include this as part of your itinerary if you happen to be staying in Ella.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The walk meanders along tea plantations and is extremely scenic. There are parts of the trail where you teeter close to the edge, but that's what makes it fun. We took about 2 hours to hike up and down, it's relatively easy, but not advisable after the rain as the slopes would be slippery and dangerous. This was one of the highlights of our 11 day trip to Sri Lanka.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My husband and I hiked Little Adam's Peak with our twin two year olds.  The hike itself was moderately strenuous, so we used two BabyErgo carriers to get them up the hill.  It was not a long hike, and there are two ways to get up: the stairs or the long windy uphill slope.  We chose to take the stairs up, and then the windy road down.  This was perfect.  The view from the top is really breathtaking, and there's enough room that we could let the kids out of the carriers to share the view and take some pictures (though be careful of sheer rock faces).  Make sure to climb up both sides of the summit, since each has a view that is a bit different, and both are beautiful.  I would recommend this with kids.  It's a relatively short hike that feels worth it.

review_text: It's a gentle 30min walk from town - amazed to see so many tourists taking a tuk tuk to get there. At the bottom of the trail is a delightful little cafe/garden store. The trail/walk is not that strenuous, along the way you'll pass some Tamil tea pickers - as long as you realise that they aren't really picking tea they are just there for tourists to take their photo & put their hand out for payment (however keep in mind that the average wage for a tea picker is Rs600).  The last bit of the trail is a bit steeper with a number of steps but the views from the top across to Ella Rock and the waterfall are spectacular and definitely worthwhile. The round trip is probably less than an hour.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It's a lovely walk to the peak, particularly once you are off the main road and walking through the tea plantations. We stopped in at Cafe 98 on the way back, which has a great vibe and view. It's fairly easy to then continue onto the Nine Arches Bridge. From the cafe, walk towards reception, turn right to walk out towards Passara Road where you then turn right. Walk past the large Newburgh Estate Green Tea factory on your right and you will come to a road junction and a small shop. Take the first left and follow that road down the hill. When you see the rail bridge on the left, take any side track to get through to the train tracks (it's a little steep so wear sturdy shoes). After the bridge and tunnel its a relatively easy walk back to Ella station along the tracks. Stop in at Ella station before you head off and take note of the train timetable so you know when to expect trains - to avoid being in their way (they are not very fast), and ideally to capture them in photos crossing the bridge.

review_text: We walked from Little Heaven Guesthouse near town, about 1km away. We enjoy the walk passing by small villages. Even though there is no sign board, we can easily ask any local and they will gladly gives us the direction. Once we get to the steps, it's just all the way up. review_text: We went on Little Adam's Peak after climbing the real Adam's Peak, just to warm our muscles from the hike two nights before. The path takes you through tea plantations and last 20 minutes you are walking up the hill (there are some stairs, but not too much). location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We went to Ella in September and stayed at the 98 Acres resort. We arrived around 6am, after the breakfast we took the short stroll from our resort to Little Adam's Peak. Best to do these hiking trips early and you climb down by 11am before hot sun. This is also called "the small adam's peak" the climb is very easy to moderate, not a difficult one at all! We saw tourists of all ages from teenagers to retired. The views are breathtaking! There are few other peaks you can climb which my partner Chamal did. However as I was recovering from a shoulder dislocation I didn't try the other peaks. There is absolutely no need to take a guide with you. Can do it on your own. On the way back, there is a shin for "beer" . This is the restaurant and bar at 98 Acres resort. Highly recommend a visit!!!! Breathtaking views and a true reward for the achievement of climbing Little Adam's Peak! Enjoy your visits and we highly recommend it!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: A lovely morning walk for about an hour that passed by tea plantations, villages and lots of stunning views. I had a dog as a guide which was absolutely cute. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Really enjoyable and easy walk from the town.  Views from the top wonderful as is the views of the tea plantations literally all around you.  If you go mid afternoon you can ofter see black eagles skimming over the plantations, and towards late afternoon dozens of bee eaters lining the telegraph wires.  Don't bother with the cafe on the left hand side about 100 metres or so before you tackle the last part of the climb - a bit overpriced.  Much better to go to the hotel/restaurant on the left after the last bit of the climb for very reasonably priced drinks and snacks, and more wonderful views.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Whoever named this hill was having a joke! It's nothing like Adam Peak, Sri Pada - not even a mini peak. You can do it both up and down without any steps if you like - my recommendation really because of the views and pace. We started the short, pleasant walk through the tea estate around 9am before it got hot, enjoying the view of Ella Rock opposite, the tea pluckers, birds and trees in flower. Fortunately we knew to go to the left of the steps and to follow the trail because the views on this side were gorgeous too. Fortunately the day was quite clear so we were lucky in how far we could see. Being early, there were only a few people at the top including one girl whose partner was pleading with her to come back on to firm ground and not stand on the edge to have her photo taken. The photo was more important to her than her partner's fear for her or her own life. We took the steps down so it was a quick descent. By this time there was a steady stream of people climbing up the stairs, most without hats or water bottles and feeling the heat quite considerably. We stopped for morning tea at the restaurant and garden nursery at the car park area. It was very pleasant with views of Ella Rock, bird avairies, clean bathroom and an extensive menu. A guesthouse there, Ella Flower Garden Resort, is also almost complete and looked like a great new place to stay.

review_text: Access is via a sandy road off the tarmac main road. Easy walk and could be accessed by wheelchair ( or push bike) for example. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam peak is not related in any way to the Adam Peak or Sri Pada which is located in Hatton District some 50 km away by rail from Ella where this Little Adam peak is located. The start off place is at the junction of the Ella -Wellayana roads. opposite the Curd Shop cafe. Its a good idea to start the morning walk with a hearty breakfast at the  Curd shop. We tried ommelet with bread, jam and butter and sipped milk tea while enjoying the street scene.  their curd with fruits is a hot favourite.  the walk is down a windy road passing villages and shops and tea plantation which produces organic tea leaves. a good 30 minutes walk bring us to the top of the adams peak . the view is good in the morning as the fog will blur the scenery in the evenings. Opposite the adam peak is the Ella rock with its bare rock face , another favourite walking trip of Ella.  We see a few tourists doing their medidation and yoga on the peak , relaxing in the wind and sunlight. it gives us a good feeling altogether . we also have a few stray  dogs  for company  , where they will show and lead the way.  after the walk its back to town for some ice cream at the newly opened supermarket right in town.  all in its about 2 hour trip.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Early morning 'hike' up to Little Adams Peak was well worth it. Avoid the heat by going early or late - as long as there's daylight you're good to go! I say hike but really it's a walk that will give you a slight work out, if the weather is good then you'll manage it in flip-flops. Walk through meandering roads from the edge of Ella, skirt through a tea plantation to the bottom of the hill. Man-made steps are steep and will get your heart rate going but it's worth it. Views from the top across the valley are stunning.  Whether you have a camera with you or not you wont forget the views in a hurry.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: My husband and I, accompanied by our guide, Krishan Fernando from TripLanka Tours, hiked to Little Adam's Peak. It is worth the climb for the spectacular views and the bird watching. It took us about an hour, as we stopped to take pictures. Go early before it gets too hot!

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The reviews were slightly deceiving and we took a path which took us no where. From 98 acres, head down the road from the reception (ask them directions) and take the 2nd turn to the left with a iron barrier/ gate and walk up the gravel road. After the first fee steps (maybe 10 - 20) there seems to be a foot path by a rock that juts out where the stairs continue. This maybe the path recommended in the reviews. We took the stairs all the way up (about a 15min walk) and were stunned at the views. Best time to visit would be 7am or 4pm. We climbed up at noon which wasnt the optimum time for good photographs.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: It takes about 30-40 mins to climb little Adam's peak with 2 young kids . We started the climb near the hotel 98 acres. The first part is a walk through the tea plantation and the last part consists of steps which are a bit steep. We were told this was the shorter path and took it because of the kids but be careful as the steps are steep and unprotected on one side ! The view is just breathtaking from the top though and well worth the climb. The kids enjoyed it thoroughly and wanted to do it all over again !

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Easy peasy stroll. 4km round trip mostly flat. Really pleasant wandering through the tea plantations. Not brilliantly signposted but you're walking past shops and houses so the locals will tea you if you've walked into their field by mistake. It was great to get our legs going again and ready for bigger walks like Workds End and Adams Peak (the real one).

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We walked up the Peak around 11am it only took 1 hour return and that was chatting to people on the way. The views are magnificent with great photo opportunities.  Walking earlier in the morning is a little cooler as it does get quite humid later in the day. The evenings in April are guaranteed to have heavy rain so an evening walk at this time of year would not be recommended especially as the Peak is surrounded by clouds.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: it took just about 2 hours and you can see the tea plantations on the way, the famous ella gap, valleys and greenery all around. there is also a green tea factory on the way which is OK, not amazing if you had visited a tea factory before. overall really lovely half day trip :)

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Little Adam's Peak was an easy hike.  Keep going once you get to the top over to the next hill where there are two big rocks jutting out.  The views are absolutely stunning.  I sat there for a couple of hours just taking it all in.  Highly recommend.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: I did this walk and loved it!  It is not difficult at all, although if someone is entirely out-of-shape, they may find some of it a little challenging (the stairs to reach the peak).  The top of the peak is beautiful, with great views and opportunities to hike further.  The little village just below is very well worth a visit.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: We went to Little Adams Peak this morning leaving around 8am. If you take a gentle stroll and stop to admire the views then you're looking at about 1.5 to 2 hours. We took the path round to the left at the steps, which meant we had a lovely gentle climb through a windy path taking us through the tea plantation which meant we saw all the local workers in action. I'd definately recommend this route to reach the top. I'm personally scared of heights but managed the climb, just left the last 10 meters or so as the summit is a bit more scary! For a quick decent then from the top take the path to the left - where most walkers appear from and then climb the stairs - it's literally about 15 mins down to the main path. Beautiful views and not at all challenging!

review_text: We used the steps to get up the hill, but were not looking forward to the descent (knees no longer like descending lots of steps!). location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: This hike is not strenuous and the view from the top is rewarding. When you have reached the foot of the top there is a recently built stairway. DO NOT TAKE IT. It is much easier to follow the path at the left side of it that will bring you to the top without shortage of breath. You can take the stairs on the way back. You will walk through a beautiful landscape with tea plantations.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: What a gorgeous stroll out of Ella, winding your way up through the tea plantations. At a gentle pace it's only an hour from town to the summit, and that includes stopping along the way to fill your camera's memory card with pictures that will never do it justice.

location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: The mountain range in the Badulla, Ella area which is considered for Small Sripada (Little Adam's Peak) has become an attraction to local and foreign tourist. A large number of people visit the area to admire its scenic beauty. Small Sripada is located about 2 km from the Ella town. From this location Kataragama and the Hambantota beach which are hundreds of kilometers away can also be seen. The Namunukula, Poonagala and Narangala mountain ranges also located on near this place. location_name: Little Adam s Peak View Point
review_text: Alone, I climb this little Adam’s Peak early morning in December. I started in the Ella centre at 5AM and followed the road until the path to the hill for 15-20 minutes. The first uphill walk was lovely since the trail is in between the tea plantation. This will go for 10-15 minutes before reaching the concrete steps that leads to the peak. My main goal is to see the sunrise as travellers describe incredible but unfortunately it rained just before I reached the top. I didn’t see the sunrise but instead I was enveloped by hazes that quickly come and go which feels awesome. Some fogs are really thick and heavy that one moment it got me scared, I was blinded and I can’t see the valley below. It is unforgettable. Love this place. I will go back to see the sunrise! Ella is special. Not because it has something listed in the wonders of the world but its simplicity is unique. Indeed, very natural!!
